SpatialThinker-7B, trained on only 7,000 samples, matches the performance of GPT-5 and surpasses GPT-4o, while the larger SpatialThinker-30B outperforms both GPT-5 and Claude 4 Sonnet across 14 spatial and real-world benchmarks. These results demonstrate that combining structured spatial grounding with reward-aligned reasoning enables robust spatial understanding with limited data, marking a significant advancement in vision-language models.

item.title: Researchers fine-tune Romanian vision-language models using parameter-efficient LoRA on translated Flickr30K dataset, improving visual QA and image captioning performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have enhanced Romanian vision-language models by translating the Flickr30K dataset into Romanian and extending it for visual question answering using open-source large language models. They fine-tuned models from the LLaMA 3.2, LLaVA 1.6, and Qwen2 families with the parameter-efficient LoRA method, resulting in improved performance on Romanian visual question answering and image captioning tasks. The seven-billion-parameter Qwen2-VL-RoVQA model achieved notable gains in BERTScore F1, with improvements of 2.29% on visual question answering and 4.45% on captioning compared to its original version. The fine-tuned models also demonstrated a significant reduction in grammatical errors, indicating enhanced language understanding and fluency in Romanian. This work addresses the resource gap in multimodal natural language processing for low-resource languages and contributes to democratizing generative AI by improving Romanian language capabilities in vision-language tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose R2PO method to decouple rollout and inference policies in LLM reasoning, improving accuracy by up to 3.4% on MATH-500 and 1.3% on APPS benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced R²PO (Residual Rollout Policy Optimization), a new method that separates the policies used for training rollouts and inference in large language model (LLM) reasoning. This approach addresses the conflict between optimizing for informative training gradients and producing accurate, consistent inference responses by adding a lightweight Residual Rollout-Head to decouple these processes. Experiments demonstrate that R²PO improves accuracy by up to 3.4% on the MATH-500 benchmark and 1.3% on the APPS benchmark compared to existing methods. The study highlights that traditional reinforcement learning methods assume the same policy should govern both training and inference, which can entangle gradients and limit exploration. By diversifying rollouts during training while maintaining inference generation, R²PO achieves more diverse training trajectories and reduces length bias. The researchers have made their code publicly available to support further development in this area.

item.title: Researchers identify Endogenous Steering Resistance in Llama-3.3-70B language model, showing 3.8% explicit recovery from activation steering misalignment with implications for AI safety [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called Endogenous Steering Resistance (ESR) in the Llama-3.3-70B language model, where the model can recover mid-generation from task-misaligned activation steering by explicitly restarting and continuing on-topic despite ongoing steering perturbations. This explicit ESR occurs at a rate of 3.8% in Llama-3.3-70B, with smaller models showing it less frequently. The study used sparse autoencoder latents to steer activations and found that zero-ablating certain latents reduced repeated attempts by 25%, indicating specific components involved in ESR. The research further demonstrated that ESR can be enhanced through meta-prompting and fine-tuning on synthetic self-correction examples. ESR has important implications for AI safety, as it may protect models against adversarial activation-space manipulation but could also hinder beneficial steering interventions, since the model cannot distinguish between harmful and helpful steering. The authors have made their code publicly available for further exploration.

item.title: Researchers propose gradient regularization to reduce reward hacking in reinforcement learning from human feedback and verifiable rewards, showing improved accuracy and performance over KL penalty methods [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a gradient regularization (GR) technique to address reward hacking in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) and verifiable rewards (RLVR) used in training modern language models. Unlike traditional methods that use a Kullback-Leibler (KL) penalty to limit policy updates, this approach biases training towards regions where the reward model is more accurate by encouraging flatter optima. The team established a theoretical link between reward accuracy and the flatness of the optimum and confirmed this correlation empirically. The study demonstrates that GR outperforms KL penalty methods across various reinforcement learning experiments with language models. GR not only achieves higher win rates as judged by GPT but also reduces issues like overfitting to reward formats and prevents manipulation of evaluation metrics in tasks where language models act as judges. This method offers a promising alternative for improving the reliability and effectiveness of reward-based training in language models.

item.title: Researchers present a data-driven pipeline that optimizes GPU efficiency for distributed LLM-adapter serving, reducing GPU requirements by 60% while avoiding request starvation and memory errors [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a data-driven pipeline that optimizes GPU efficiency for distributed serving of Large Language Model (LLM) adapters, reducing the number of GPUs required by 60% while preventing request starvation and memory errors. The pipeline calculates the optimal adapter placement for a given workload by accurately predicting maximum feasible throughput on each GPU, enabling near-peak utilization with minimal resources. The approach combines a Digital Twin that simulates system dynamics with high accuracy, a distilled machine learning model trained on data generated by the Digital Twin, and a greedy placement algorithm that uses these performance estimates to maximize GPU usage. This method achieves throughput estimation errors below 5% and runs significantly faster than traditional benchmarking, supporting both predictable and unpredictable workloads. Beyond improving GPU efficiency, the pipeline is adaptable to other objectives such as minimizing latency, making it a versatile solution for future large-scale LLM serving infrastructures.

item.title: Researchers introduce SpreadsheetArena to evaluate LLM-generated spreadsheets via blind preference votes, revealing variability in style and alignment with domain best practices [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SpreadsheetArena, a platform designed to evaluate language models' ability to generate spreadsheets based on natural language prompts. The platform uses blind pairwise preference voting to assess the quality of spreadsheet workbooks produced by large language models (LLMs), highlighting the variability in stylistic, structural, and functional features across different prompts. This approach addresses the unique challenges of spreadsheet generation, which involves well-defined, multi-dimensional outputs with complex interactivity and layout considerations. Expert evaluations, particularly in finance-related prompts, indicate that even top-performing models often fail to produce spreadsheets that align with domain-specific best practices. SpreadsheetArena is hosted live and includes a publicly released dataset of prompts, generated spreadsheets, and preference votes, aiming to support further research into spreadsheet generation as a complex and open-ended task for LLMs.

item.title: Researchers find large language models generate harmful responses via a distinct, shared mechanism across harm types, with alignment compressing harmful weights but causing brittle safety [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have discovered that large language models (LLMs) generate harmful responses through a distinct and shared internal mechanism across different types of harm. Their study shows that harmful content production relies on a compact set of model weights that are separate from those responsible for benign functions. Alignment training compresses these harmful weights, reshaping the model's internal representations of harmfulness, but this also leads to brittle safety measures that can be bypassed or cause broad misalignment when fine-tuned on specific domains. Using targeted weight pruning, the researchers demonstrated that pruning harmful weights in a narrow domain significantly reduces emergent misalignment, suggesting a coherent internal structure for harmfulness in LLMs. Notably, the ability of LLMs to generate harmful content is distinct from their capacity to recognize and explain such content. These findings provide a foundation for developing more principled and robust approaches to improving the safety of large language models.

item.title: Researchers propose Kwai Summary Attention to reduce long-sequence modeling costs by compressing historical contexts into learnable summary tokens, addressing quadratic complexity in softmax attention [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Kwai Summary Attention (KSA), a new attention mechanism designed to reduce the computational costs of modeling long sequences in large language models. KSA addresses the quadratic time complexity of standard softmax attention by compressing historical context into learnable summary tokens, enabling more efficient handling of long-range dependencies without sacrificing interpretability or completeness. Traditional approaches to managing long sequences either reduce the key-value cache size or use architectures optimized for cache efficiency, but these methods often involve trade-offs between memory usage and modeling effectiveness. KSA offers an intermediate solution by maintaining a linear relationship between cache size and sequence length while applying semantic-level compression, balancing memory costs with the retention of important long-distance information. This development is significant for advancing next-generation language models, particularly in areas requiring extensive context understanding such as semantic reasoning, code intelligence, and recommendation systems. By improving efficiency in long-context scenarios, KSA has the potential to enhance both training and inference performance for extremely long sequences.

item.title: Researchers propose MemTrace framework to trace and attribute errors in large language model memory systems, introducing MemTraceBench and an automatic attribution method that improves task performance by up to 7.62% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MemTrace, a novel framework designed to trace and attribute errors in memory systems of large language models (LLMs). By converting memory pipelines into executable memory evolution graphs, MemTrace enables detailed tracking of information flow and identifies the root causes of failures. The team also developed MemTraceBench, a benchmark derived from various memory systems, to systematically analyze memory failure modes and introduced an automatic attribution method that improves task performance by up to 7.62% through guided prompt optimization. The study reveals that memory failures in LLMs are often systematic, resulting from issues such as information loss and retrieval misalignment at the operation level. By leveraging fine-grained attribution signals, the framework establishes a closed-loop system that automatically corrects faults, enhancing the reliability and effectiveness of LLM memory systems. The researchers plan to release the code publicly to support further development and debugging in this area.

item.title: Researchers present ResearchClawBench, a benchmark evaluating autonomous scientific research across 40 tasks in 10 domains, revealing current AI agents' limited re-discovery capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced ResearchClawBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the autonomous scientific research capabilities of AI agents across 40 tasks spanning 10 scientific domains. Each task is based on a real published paper and includes related literature and raw data, with the target paper hidden during evaluation to test the AI's ability to independently rediscover scientific findings. The benchmark uses expert-curated rubrics to assess performance, allowing for both re-discovery and novel insights. The study assessed seven autonomous research agents and seventeen large language models (LLMs) using a unified protocol. Results showed that current AI systems struggle with reliable re-discovery, with the top autonomous agent scoring an average of 21.5 and the best LLM scoring 20.7 out of a possible frontier mean of 26.5. Analysis revealed common failures in matching experimental protocols, evidence, and core scientific concepts. ResearchClawBench establishes a reproducible framework for measuring progress toward fully autonomous scientific research, highlighting the significant challenges that remain before AI can independently conduct reliable scientific investigations.

item.title: Researchers formulate hallucination onset detection as quickest change detection, achieving detection delays of 11-13 tokens with learned CUSUM statistics versus 31 tokens for baseline methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have reframed the detection of hallucination onset in language models as a quickest change detection problem, achieving significantly faster detection times compared to traditional methods. By modeling the latent faithful or hallucinated state as a first-order Markov process and applying classical change-point theory, they established a theoretical lower bound on detection delay. Their approach uses a causal recurrent labeler functioning as a CUSUM detector with learned increments, reducing detection delays to 11-13 tokens versus 31 tokens for a linear baseline, although low false-alarm rates still limit recall and increase delay. The study reveals that the improved speed primarily stems from better per-token scoring rather than temporal accumulation. An information-rate optimality analysis shows that the learned scoring captures only a fraction of the available divergence in features, indicating room for improvement. This work highlights the limitations of standard classification metrics in capturing detection delay and demonstrates how sequential analysis can provide a more precise measure of hallucination onset detection performance.

item.title: Researchers find language models with lossy memory produce confident errors while empty memory leads to abstention, proposing a source-first policy to restore correctability across models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that language models with lossy memory-where incorrect conclusions are retained but the underlying reasoning is lost-tend to produce confident errors, whereas models with empty memory often abstain from answering. This phenomenon, termed brittle memory, arises because answers cannot be recomputed without their original inputs. The study shows that whether a model confidently errs or abstains depends on its disposition rather than its capability. The researchers introduced a reclaim evaluation method to measure correctability, revealing that preserving the source information rather than just the final answer is crucial for enabling corrections across different models. The team proposed a simple source-first policy that retains the recomputable source data while discarding the derived conclusion, which significantly improves correctability without increasing memory budget. They tested this approach across various models and real dialogue datasets, identifying conditions where the fix may fail, such as large source size or noise. Their findings highlight the importance of memory design in language models and provide tools and benchmarks to assess and improve model reliability in handling memory and corrections.

item.title: Kapa.ai uses a small LLM to prune 68% of RAG context while retaining 96% recall, reducing query costs by a third in AI assistants for large knowledge bases [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Kapa.ai has developed a method to reduce the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) context by 68% while maintaining 96% recall, significantly cutting query costs for AI assistants handling large knowledge bases. Their approach introduces a small, cost-effective language model that evaluates and prunes irrelevant chunks of information before passing data to the main, more expensive model, optimizing both performance and expense. This pruning step addresses the inefficiency of traditional retrieval systems that pass many unnecessary chunks to the generator, which increases costs without improving answers. By assessing the relevance of all retrieved chunks collectively rather than individually, Kapa.ai's solution ensures that only essential information is retained, improving cost efficiency without sacrificing answer quality. The innovation allows AI assistants to manage large and complex product knowledge bases more effectively, enabling tighter context management and reducing the computational load. This advancement could influence future designs of retrieval and generation pipelines in AI systems, balancing recall and cost more effectively.

item.title: Researchers propose ASK+, a trajectory-aware uncertainty-gated LLM assistance method that improves reinforcement learning success under partial observability across multiple environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ASK+, a method that enhances reinforcement learning agents operating under partial observability by integrating trajectory-aware context and structured reasoning into small language model (SLM) assistance. This approach addresses the limitations of previous uncertainty-gated methods, which rarely allowed SLMs to contribute independently due to insufficient contextual information. ASK+ provides the SLM with a partially revealed map, visited positions, and action history, enabling it to act as an informative consultant that occasionally corrects the agent's policy, leading to improved performance across multiple environments. The study demonstrates that the predictive entropy signal used for selective querying effectively measures action uncertainty rather than state uncertainty, maintaining its usefulness in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs). ASK+ achieved notable success rates, including 93% on DoorKey, 70% on FourRooms, and 73.7% accuracy on HigherLower, matching or exceeding benchmarks set by larger models. These results highlight that prompt design and selective gating have a greater impact than model scale, enabling effective guidance without relying on large language models.

item.title: Researchers introduce Incognita framework to evaluate generative agents in socially distributed task environments with 540 trials showing limited success and behavior insights [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Incognita, a new framework designed to evaluate generative agents in socially distributed task environments where knowledge and actions are partitioned among role-specific participants. This framework separates social interaction from grounded execution, allowing agents to communicate with specialists who mediate permissible operations, which are then executed in a controlled environment. The study tested three generative agent models across 18 tasks with 540 trials, revealing limited success rates but notable behavioral insights such as increased knowledge elicitation and interaction with multiple entities. Incognita-Retail adapts an existing retail benchmark into a multi-entity setting while maintaining consistent reward structures. The evaluation showed progress in agent performance, with success rates improving from 0% to up to 17.2% and reductions in premature task completion. Despite these advances, the agents' reliability remains low, highlighting challenges in achieving effective agency in complex social environments. These findings suggest that socially distributed task environments provide valuable opportunities to observe agent behaviors like knowledge gathering, source selection, and action attempts before consistent success is achieved. The research underscores the importance of such environments for advancing the development and assessment of generative agents in realistic social contexts.

item.title: Researchers propose cross-survey transfer to evaluate large language models simulating survey respondents, achieving 52% accuracy on unseen items in Taiwan Election and Democratization Study 2024 data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a new evaluation method called cross-survey transfer to assess large language models (LLMs) simulating human survey respondents. Using data from the Taiwan Election and Democratization Study 2024, they tested three open-weight LLMs and found that zero-shot models achieved 52% accuracy in predicting answers to unseen survey items, approaching the performance of supervised machine learning models. This approach offers a more rigorous test of LLMs' ability to predict individual responses rather than just matching overall data patterns. The study revealed a hierarchy in predictability across different survey constructs, with partisan attitudes being the most predictable and sovereignty issues the least. It also found that common LLM limitations, such as variance collapse and safety alignment effects, are more complex than previously thought, affecting both supervised and unsupervised models differently. These findings highlight both the potential and limitations of using LLMs for silicon sampling in survey research.

item.title: Researchers study agentic AI policy repair using region-level feedback in hotel-pricing simulation, finding that aggregate alignment metrics can mislead evaluation without per-state expert actions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers investigated the challenge of evaluating agentic AI systems that edit decision policies without access to per-state expert action labels. Using a hotel-pricing simulator, they tested a policy editor that received only region-level feedback on price distribution differences from a benchmark policy, without observing benchmark actions or outcomes. The editor, based on a large language model, achieved revenue per available room (RevPAR) close to the benchmark, demonstrating effective policy repair despite limited feedback. The study found that simple aggregate alignment metrics can be misleading, as the editor's improvements were not solely due to revenue gains but also to better alignment with episode composition. Comparisons with other editing methods showed that semantic understanding and region-error correspondence were crucial for successful policy repair. The results suggest that evaluating agentic policy repair should focus on whether diagnostic feedback reliably translates into improved outcomes, rather than relying on single behavioral distance measures.

item.title: Researchers develop end-to-end analytics framework using mobile data for large-scale urban mobility analysis and decision support with Google BigQuery, Vertex AI, and Power BI [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an end-to-end analytics framework that leverages real-time mobile location data to analyze urban mobility and support decision-making in areas such as tourism, transportation, and retail. The framework integrates advanced technologies including Google BigQuery, Vertex AI, and Power BI to process data, build machine learning models, and visualize insights. It addresses challenges like tourism planning, parking management, bus route optimization, and commercial strategy through a modular architecture that supports multiple stakeholder use cases. The platform employs data anonymization and ETL pipelines to ensure privacy and efficiency, while its analytical models perform tasks such as mobility profiling, trajectory mining, area of influence analysis, traffic anomaly detection, and origin-destination pattern analysis. The results demonstrate the system's capability to capture detailed user mobility patterns at fine spatial and temporal scales, providing actionable insights for urban planners and business strategists.

item.title: arXiv:2607.03561 presents doubly-efficient single-prover interactive proofs for AI safety, enabling scalable verification without debate under oracle-aided computations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The paper arXiv:2607.03561 introduces a new approach to AI safety verification by developing doubly-efficient single-prover interactive proofs that do not rely on the traditional debate model involving two competing AI models. This method addresses limitations of debate-based verification, which assumes equal abilities and truthfulness among provers, by enabling scalable verification even when computations access oracles such as human judgment or external databases. The authors present interactive proofs suitable for oracle-aided computations under conditions where the computation is robust to some incorrect oracle responses or when the oracle is represented by a low-degree polynomial. These results demonstrate that interactive verification of AI outputs can be achieved without debate, offering a more practical and noise-tolerant framework for ensuring AI alignment with human intentions.

item.title: Researchers propose an explainable reinforcement learning framework for adaptive traffic signal control that preserves intersection topology and ensures safety compliance, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in simulations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an explainable reinforcement learning framework for adaptive traffic signal control that maintains the structural topology of intersections and ensures safety compliance. This approach disaggregates real-time traffic data into distinct lane entities and phase configurations, using a dual-stage attention network to capture relational dependencies and inter-lane conflicts. The system integrates a deterministic action-masking mechanism to prevent unsafe signal transitions, achieving superior performance in delay reduction compared to existing methods in simulation. The framework provides full visual and analytical interpretability through an affinity matrix that quantifies the influence of signal phases on traffic volumes and queues, aligning with established traffic engineering principles. This transparency addresses challenges related to the black-box nature of deep reinforcement learning models, facilitating regulatory compliance, operational trust, and easier troubleshooting. The architecture offers a promising, auditable solution for next-generation adaptive traffic control systems.

item.title: Researchers propose an online linear programming framework for multi-objective routing in large language model serving, improving latency and throughput under batch-size and KV-cache constraints [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an online linear programming framework to optimize routing in large language model (LLM) serving, addressing the challenge of dispatching sequential requests to parallel decode workers under strict batch-size and KV-cache constraints. This multi-objective optimization approach improves control over latency and throughput trade-offs by using a bid-price control policy that admits requests based on service-level objectives (SLOs) and shadow prices. The method achieves millisecond decision times through warm-started, projected first-order updates that track evolving dual shadow prices efficiently. The framework was integrated into the Vidur simulator, where it demonstrated significant performance gains over traditional heuristic routing methods across various SLO regimes, including end-to-end latency, time-to-first-token, throughput, and tail latency. This science-based approach offers a more effective alternative to heuristic routing, providing interpretable decision rewards and predictable runtime in LLM serving environments.

item.title: Researchers propose a clustering-based unsupervised framework using K-Means++ to identify suspicious trading patterns in one million capital market transactions from 2012 to 2024 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an unsupervised fraud-detection framework using K-Means++ clustering to identify suspicious trading patterns in capital markets. Analyzing approximately one million financial transactions from 2012 to 2024, the method flagged 2.02% of trades as suspicious, categorizing them into types such as spoofing, pump and dump, insider trading, and fake breakouts, with nearly half remaining unclassified. The model's effectiveness is supported by a Silhouette Score of 0.561, despite the absence of ground truth data. The study applies heuristic thresholds based on market practices to classify fraudulent trades within the clustered data. Among the suspicious trades, 51.10% were identified as spoofing, 0.10% as pump and dump schemes, 0.55% as insider trading, and 1.43% as fake breakouts. This clustering-based approach offers a scalable tool for detecting market manipulation, which undermines confidence in trading platforms.

item.title: Researchers develop YAACS, a server-side deep learning system for aimbot detection in FPS games achieving 88.6% accuracy and 0.97% false positive rate using stacked LSTM models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed YAACS, a server-side deep learning system designed to detect aimbot cheating in multiplayer first-person shooter (FPS) games. YAACS uses a stacked LSTM model trained on time-series and behavioral gameplay data to distinguish between regular players and those using aimbots, achieving an accuracy of 88.6% with a false positive rate of 0.97%. This approach outperforms traditional decision tree methods by significantly reducing false accusations while maintaining high detection accuracy. The system analyzes features such as aim velocity, number of shots, distance to target, utility usage, and player movement patterns, integrating these into a classifier that can be embedded within game servers. By leveraging temporal sequence modeling, YAACS captures the dynamic context of player behavior, which is critical for minimizing incorrect cheat detections and ensuring fair gameplay in increasingly complex FPS environments.

item.title: Researchers use Truncated Reasoning AUC Evaluation to detect answer-driven reasoning in LLM-based educational tutors, finding answer keys make correct answers available early in explanations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a method called Truncated Reasoning AUC Evaluation (TRACE) to detect when large language model (LLM) tutors produce explanations that are answer-driven rather than derived from the student-facing problem. By testing 1,000 math problems under different tutoring contexts-including access to correct or incorrect answer keys-they found that having the answer key available allows the model to produce the correct answer very early in its explanation, often within the first 10% of the reasoning steps. This suggests that the model's explanations may rely on the answer key rather than genuine problem-solving. The study used the Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct model and showed that access to the answer key significantly increased the median TRACE AUC score from 0.375 to 0.900, indicating earlier availability of the correct answer in the explanation. This effect persisted even in cases where both question-only and answer-key explanations ended with the correct answer. These findings support the use of truncated chain-of-thought auditing as a lightweight diagnostic tool to identify answer-driven reasoning in educational LLM tutors, which has implications for the design and evaluation of AI-based tutoring systems.

item.title: DSpark introduces confidence-scheduled speculative decoding with semi-autoregressive generation to accelerate large language model inference and improve throughput by up to 85% in live serving systems [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: DSpark is a new speculative decoding framework designed to accelerate large language model (LLM) inference by combining high-throughput parallel generation with adaptive, load-aware verification. It uses a semi-autoregressive architecture to maintain draft quality by modeling dependencies within token blocks and employs confidence-scheduled verification to dynamically adjust verification length based on predicted token acceptance, improving efficiency in high-concurrency serving systems. In offline benchmarks, DSpark outperforms state-of-the-art autoregressive and parallel drafters by significantly increasing the accepted token length. When integrated into the DeepSeek-V4 serving system under live traffic, it reduces verification waste and boosts per-user generation speeds by 60 to 85 percent compared to the existing production baseline, enabling higher performance tiers and improving overall system throughput without sacrificing interactivity.

item.title: Researchers find privileged on-policy self-distillation reduces accuracy by up to 17% in thinking models on long reasoning tasks across multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that using privileged on-policy self-distillation, where a language model teaches itself using additional information like problem solutions, can reduce accuracy by up to 17% in advanced thinking models during long reasoning tasks. This effect was observed across multiple models and benchmarks, including Qwen3 and OLMo models tested on AIME24, AIME25, and HMMT25 datasets. The accuracy drop is linked to how the privileged context influences learning at decision points with multiple possible reasoning paths, particularly affecting models during extended reasoning sequences where they typically perform best. The study highlights that while on-policy distillation generally improves thinking models, adding privileged information reverses these gains by lowering the diversity of reasoning paths and penalizing reconsideration steps. This contrasts with instruction-tuned models, which benefit from privileged context. The findings suggest that self-distillation methods for strong reasoning models need careful attention to token-level signals, especially around correction and verification steps, to avoid impairing their problem-solving abilities.

item.title: Researchers propose SiamixFormer, a fully-transformer Siamese network with temporal fusion for improved building and change detection in bi-temporal remote sensing images [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SiamixFormer, a fully-transformer Siamese network designed to improve building detection and change detection in bi-temporal remote sensing images. Unlike traditional models that rely solely on pre-disaster images, SiamixFormer processes both pre- and post-disaster images using two encoders and a hierarchical transformer architecture. This approach incorporates temporal transformers for feature fusion, enhancing the model's ability to maintain large receptive fields and effectively analyze changes over time. The model generates queries from pre-disaster images and keys and values from post-disaster images, allowing temporal features to be integrated during fusion. Outputs from the temporal transformer are decoded by a simple MLP at each stage. Evaluations on datasets such as xBD, WHU, LEVIR-CD, and CDD demonstrate that SiamixFormer outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both building detection and change detection tasks.

item.title: Survey classifies over 30 key-value cache management systems for large language model serving, identifying five architectural archetypes and highlighting open problems in distributed memory hierarchies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent survey examines over thirty key-value (KV) cache management systems used in large language model (LLM) serving, categorizing them along four dimensions: locality, lifetime, ownership, and substrate. This classification reveals five main architectural archetypes-local-paged, disaggregated-pipeline, shared-store, memory-pool, and hybrid-tier-and highlights how ownership significantly influences design differences in distributed systems once workload and hardware are fixed. The study also reviews current evaluation methods and identifies seven missing KV-specific metrics, connecting these gaps to unresolved challenges in areas such as fault tolerance, isolation, tiered eviction, speculative decoding, mixture-of-experts serving, and shared-cache semantics. By providing a comprehensive framework for understanding KV cache architectures and pinpointing evaluation shortcomings, the survey offers valuable insights for advancing distributed memory hierarchies in LLM serving. It underscores the importance of addressing these open problems to improve system robustness and efficiency in managing KV caches across diverse hardware and workload scenarios.

item.title: Researchers present Homer, a hierarchical memory and agentic reasoning framework that improves understanding of long-form videos by enabling multi-scale memory retrieval and causal reasoning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Homer, a hierarchical memory and agentic reasoning framework designed to improve the understanding of long-form videos by enabling multi-scale memory retrieval and causal reasoning. Unlike existing methods that either use compact visual representations lacking semantic depth or organize memory based on temporal proximity without explicit causal links, Homer structures memory to reflect the multi-scale nature of long videos, from raw perception to events connected by temporal and causal relations. Its agentic reasoner mimics human exploration by locating relevant scenes, retrieving details, and composing answers through iterative memory retrieval with verification and correction at each step. Homer demonstrated significant performance improvements over previous methods, achieving higher scores on benchmarks such as M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web, and Video-MME-Long. It also consistently enhanced the capabilities of various large language model backbones, indicating its model-agnostic potential for grounded retrieval and multi-hop narrative reasoning in processing hour-long videos under limited memory constraints.

item.title: Researchers introduce Fusion, a unified adaptive inference framework for Vision Transformers that coordinates token merging, early exiting, and pruning to reduce energy use by 48% and improve calibration on ImageNet-1k [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Fusion, a unified adaptive inference framework for Vision Transformers that integrates token merging, early exiting, and token pruning to enhance efficiency and accuracy. Fusion processes tokens in a staged manner-merging tokens first, then evaluating confidence, and finally pruning tokens only for samples continuing inference-allowing these mechanisms to work cooperatively. This approach reduces inference energy consumption by 48% and improves calibration error by up to four times on ImageNet-1k, while maintaining or surpassing the performance of existing adaptive Vision Transformer methods. Fusion includes lightweight routing modules that adjust compression strength based on each input and enable real-time tuning of the accuracy-latency trade-off without retraining. The framework demonstrates consistent transferability across multiple datasets and Vision Transformer backbones without requiring dataset-specific tuning, highlighting its versatility and potential for broader application in efficient image classification tasks.

item.title: Researchers present QuantFlow, a federated Mamba-based foundation model for time-series forecasting that supports privacy and uncertainty across diverse datasets including cryptocurrency and weather [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed QuantFlow, a federated foundation model designed for time-series forecasting that emphasizes privacy and uncertainty management. This model integrates inverted sequence embedding, bidirectional Mamba state-space decoders, quantile regression, and federated learning to handle diverse datasets such as cryptocurrency, traffic, electricity, influenza, and weather data without centralizing sensitive information. QuantFlow processes each variable across the entire observation window in both forward and reverse directions, projecting results to multiple conditional quantiles to improve forecasting accuracy. QuantFlow employs TSMixup, a technique that enhances temporal diversity while maintaining sequence structure, and demonstrates strong performance with mean squared errors of 0.2834 on the ETTm1 dataset and 0.2218 on weather data. In a federated setting with 20 clients and non-identically distributed data, the model maintained useful accuracy after only three communication rounds, highlighting its potential for scalable and privacy-conscious applications. However, the study also notes challenges in handling irregular epidemiological signals and long-horizon forecasting, indicating areas for future improvement.

item.title: Researchers apply federated learning to drone object detection, achieving up to 67.8% mAP improvement without centralizing data on KIIT-MiTA dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a federated learning approach for object detection in drone systems, allowing drones to collaboratively improve a shared model without centralizing sensitive image data. Using the KIIT-MiTA dataset and the Sherpa.ai federated learning platform, their method achieved significant improvements in mean Average Precision (mAP), with the lightweight YOLO26 nano model showing up to 67.8% relative gain compared to single-drone training. This approach addresses privacy, regulatory, and bandwidth challenges inherent in centralized data collection for distributed drone deployments. The study compared federated learning with single-drone and centralized training baselines, demonstrating that federated learning closely matches centralized performance while preserving data privacy. The results highlight the potential for scalable, high-performing, and privacy-preserving object detection across distributed drone fleets, even on limited edge infrastructure, without the need to transfer large volumes of aerial imagery to a central server.

item.title: Researchers propose generator-agnostic method to improve synthetic image utility by selecting diverse subsets, reducing samples by up to 40% without retraining [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a generator-agnostic method to enhance the utility of synthetic images by selecting diverse subsets from a fixed pool of generated data. This approach addresses a common bias in modern generative models, which tend to overproduce typical class modes while underrepresenting intra-class variation. By dividing each real class into homogeneous and heterogeneous subsets and applying a fidelity-diversity scoring criterion, the method improves downstream performance without requiring retraining or generator-specific adjustments. The technique consistently outperforms existing data selection baselines across multiple benchmarks, achieving comparable results to real data with up to 40% fewer synthetic samples. It remains effective even when applied to stronger, task-tuned generators, benefiting both classification and segmentation tasks. This post-generation selection strategy complements advances in generative models by enhancing the quality and efficiency of synthetic training data.

item.title: Researchers introduce a synthetic diagnostic framework using image generative models to evaluate and improve aerial-view vehicle detectors, achieving up to 13% AP50 gains with targeted real data supplementation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a synthetic diagnostic framework that uses large-scale image generative models to evaluate and improve aerial-view vehicle detectors. This framework combines text-guided image generation, attribute-controlled editing, and automated verification to create a controllable synthetic testbed, enabling detailed assessment of pretrained detectors across diverse scenes and conditions that are hard to isolate in real datasets. Testing across multiple detection architectures and real aerial datasets showed that synthetic performance trends closely match real-world weaknesses, allowing targeted data supplementation that improved detection accuracy by up to 13% AP50 with fewer additional samples than traditional augmentation methods. The approach leverages controlled synthetic probing to identify performance gaps and guide efficient data collection, demonstrating its potential as a diagnostic tool beyond conventional data augmentation. The modular framework can integrate alternative generative or vision-language models as technology advances, offering a flexible platform for ongoing improvements in aerial object detection. The researchers have made their code and datasets publicly available to support further development in this area.

item.title: Researchers present a multimodal NLP framework using XLM-RoBERTa and CLIP for early detection of fake news and violence-prone mob activity with 98% accuracy on Bangla and English datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multilingual, multimodal Natural Language Processing (NLP) framework that combines XLM-RoBERTa for text analysis and CLIP for visual embedding to detect fake news and violence-prone mob activity with 98% accuracy. The system was tested on a fused dataset of over 138,000 Bangla and English samples, integrating additional features like sarcasm detection and geospatial metadata to enhance early warning capabilities. This approach addresses the rapid spread of misinformation on social media platforms, which has been linked to real-world unrest and violence, particularly in South Asia. The framework uses a multi-head attention mechanism to fuse textual and visual data, improving detection performance beyond traditional methods. Experiments on a stratified subset of the dataset demonstrated strong precision and recall, highlighting the effectiveness of combining multiple data modalities and auxiliary signals. The inclusion of geospatial information is particularly valuable for anticipating potential escalation of misinformation into physical conflict. This research underscores the potential of advanced multimodal NLP techniques to provide timely alerts about misinformation and related social risks, offering a tool to help mitigate the impact of false information before it leads to harm. The findings suggest that integrating diverse data sources can significantly improve early detection systems, which is critical given the speed at which misinformation can spread compared to fact-checking efforts.

item.title: Researchers introduce RiskAverseOOD benchmark showing risk aversion learned by Qwen3-8B language model at low stakes generalizes partially to astronomically high stakes across multiple model scales and families [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced RiskAverseOOD, a benchmark designed to evaluate how well risk aversion learned by AI language models generalizes from low-stakes to extremely high-stakes scenarios. Their study focused on the Qwen3-8B model, demonstrating that risk-averse behavior trained on low-risk situations can partially extend to decisions involving astronomically higher stakes, with significant increases in choosing safer options compared to baseline rates. This effect was observed across different model sizes and families, including Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-14B, Gemma-3-12B-IT, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The researchers applied various training methods such as supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and activation steering to induce risk aversion. Their fine-tuned reward model also showed high accuracy in distinguishing risk-averse reasoning from risk-neutral or overly risk-averse alternatives. Despite these promising results, the generalization of risk aversion is not yet consistent enough to serve as a reliable safety mechanism, highlighting the need for further research to achieve dependable risk-averse AI behavior at all stakes.

item.title: Researchers introduce Gemma 4, a new generation of open-weight multimodal language models with 2.3B to 31B parameters, featuring improved encoders, unified architecture, and reasoning capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Gemma 4, a new generation of open-weight, multimodal language models ranging from 2.3 billion to 31 billion parameters. The Gemma 4 suite features both dense and Mixture-of-Experts architectures, improved vision and audio encoders, and a unified, encoder-free design for the 12 billion parameter model that processes raw audio and image patches. It also includes a thinking mode that allows the models to generate reasoning traces before responding, enhancing their reasoning capabilities. The design improvements in Gemma 4 focus on increasing compute efficiency, inference speed, memory usage, and long-context understanding. These advancements result in significant performance gains across STEM, multimodal, and long-context benchmarks, positioning Gemma 4 to rival larger, state-of-the-art open models in human-rated tasks.

item.title: Researchers present CoC-Seduce benchmark assessing rule adherence and vulnerability to rhetorical injection attacks in LLMs acting as adjudicators in semi-open textual game environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CoC-Seduce, a benchmark designed to evaluate how well large language models (LLMs) adhere to rules and resist rhetorical injection attacks when acting as adjudicators in semi-open textual game environments. These environments, based on Tabletop Role-Playing Game mechanics, require models to enforce explicit rules while interacting entirely through natural language. The study tested 20 adjudicator models against adversarial inputs generated by leading models like GPT-5.4, revealing that neither larger model size nor explicit reasoning guarantees robustness, with pseudo-logical reasoning identified as the primary attack method.

item.title: Researchers find large language models struggle to apply Cognitive Behavioral Therapy effectively despite high theoretical knowledge, showing bias toward validation and reflection strategies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that large language models (LLMs), despite demonstrating strong theoretical knowledge of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) with up to 96% accuracy on licensing exam questions, struggle to apply CBT effectively in practice. These models tend to default to validation and reflection responses regardless of the user's actual needs, indicating a gap between knowledge and practical application. The study introduces a knowledge-guided framework that decomposes user narratives into structured cognitive concepts and employs a Multiple Chain-of-Thought strategy to guide response selection among validation, Socratic questioning, or alternative perspectives. The researchers developed a behavior-level metric called Protocol Leverage Force (F) to measure how much an intervention shifts an LLM's default response. Testing across three open-weight LLMs and 14 case studies derived from real CBT sessions showed that simple prompting with protocol definitions did not significantly change model behavior. While the Multiple Chain-of-Thought approach improved strategy selection slightly, the effect remained minimal, with all models still biased toward validation and reflection. These findings highlight that possessing CBT knowledge alone does not ensure effective therapeutic application, providing tools for the affective computing community to better assess and address these limitations in LLMs.

item.title: Researchers introduce SPLIT, a training-free AI-generated and partially edited video detector using spatial patch-level incoherence and temporal roughness, achieving top performance at 0.1% false positive rate across three benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SPLIT, a training-free detector designed to identify AI-generated and partially edited videos with an ultra-low false positive rate, crucial for real-world applications to avoid misclassifying authentic content. SPLIT analyzes spatial patch-level incoherence and temporal roughness using patch tokens from a frozen vision encoder, combining two complementary signals-Two-step Temporal Roughness and Local Spatial Motion Incoherence-to effectively distinguish real from fake videos. The method employs a multiplicative fusion with gamma correction to enhance detection accuracy at strict thresholds and introduces a service-aligned evaluation protocol focusing on Fake Recall at a fixed false positive rate. Tested across three benchmarks-FakeParts, GenVideo, and ViF-Bench-SPLIT outperforms both supervised and other training-free detectors, maintaining robustness against post-processing while requiring minimal computational overhead. The code for SPLIT is publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers introduce Bootstrap Flow-Map-Tree sampling framework for efficient online feedback-driven global search and alignment under sampling budget constraints [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Bootstrap Flow-Map-Tree (BFMT), a new sampling framework designed to optimize global search and alignment under limited sampling budgets by leveraging sequential feedback. BFMT enables efficient, history-aware exploration by constructing full tree paths from any depth with a single function evaluation, reducing computational costs while guiding sampling decisions. This approach allows a smooth transition from broad exploration to focused refinement of promising regions, addressing challenges faced by existing methods that typically perform local searches and struggle when preferences are unknown in advance. Extensive experiments across various search and alignment tasks demonstrate that BFMT significantly outperforms baseline methods. Its dynamic scheduling of transition time steps ensures efficient allocation of sampling resources, making it a promising tool for scientific and engineering domains where maximizing discovery within constrained budgets is critical.

item.title: Researchers propose PROMPTPET, an LLM-based agent that optimizes prompt obfuscation to balance privacy and utility in AI chatbot interactions using reinforcement learning [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PROMPTPET, an AI agent that enhances privacy in chatbot interactions by optimizing how sensitive information in user prompts is obfuscated. This system balances the tradeoff between protecting user privacy and maintaining the utility of chatbot responses by selecting from four obfuscation methods-redaction, abstraction, replacement, and a novel noising/denoising technique-using a reinforcement learning-based approach. PROMPTPET evaluates each sensitive part of a prompt to apply the most effective obfuscation, ensuring useful and personalized chatbot replies while minimizing the risk of user profiling. The approach incorporates a data type taxonomy to identify sensitive information and explicitly considers the quality of chatbot responses when deciding how to obfuscate. Tested on real-world chat data, PROMPTPET matches or exceeds the privacy-utility tradeoffs achieved by any single obfuscation method and outperforms previous state-of-the-art techniques, marking a significant advancement in user-side privacy protection for AI chatbots.

item.title: Researchers propose PRECEDE, a precedent-guided AI co-scientist for side-effect-aware drug redesign using biomedical knowledge graphs and human review checkpoints [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PRECEDE, an AI system designed to assist in drug redesign by reducing specific side effects while maintaining therapeutic effectiveness. Unlike traditional methods that generate molecules in isolation, PRECEDE uses evidence-based reasoning over drug-side-effect relationships, biomedical knowledge graphs, and prior examples of safety-focused optimization. The process is guided by a large language model orchestrator and includes human review checkpoints to ensure transparency and scientific rigor. PRECEDE operates as a human-supervised AI workflow where hypotheses are auditable and grounded in established pharmacological knowledge. This approach aims to enhance drug safety by integrating computational reasoning with expert oversight, potentially improving the drug development process by making it more precise and accountable.

item.title: Researchers propose Hierarchical Landmark Sparse Attention for large language models, enabling over 64× context length extrapolation with efficiency and performance beyond full attention [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Hierarchical Landmark Sparse (HiLS) Attention, a new chunk-wise sparse attention mechanism designed to scale large language models (LLMs) to much longer contexts efficiently. HiLS Attention learns chunk selection end-to-end using the language-modeling loss, enabling it to factorize attention hierarchically and fuse outputs based on retrieval scores. This approach achieves performance comparable to or better than full attention on in-domain context lengths while extrapolating over 64 times the training context length with high retrieval accuracy. HiLS Attention also allows existing full-attention models to be converted with lightweight continued pretraining, preserving their original performance while gaining ultra-long-context capabilities. By combining sparse key-value access and computation with end-to-end retrieval learning, HiLS Attention overcomes the typical trade-off between efficiency and performance, enabling more effective and efficient long-context LLMs for general tasks than traditional full-attention models.

item.title: Researchers present CONFLUX, a latent diffusion model with reinforcement learning post-training for 3D chest CT synthesis, releasing a 200k synthetic dataset with clinical conditioning metadata [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CONFLUX, a latent diffusion model designed to generate high-quality 3D chest CT images conditioned on clinical metadata such as abnormality findings, sex, age, and reconstruction kernel. The model uses a 3D variational autoencoder to compress volumes and a rectified-flow transformer to generate images in latent space, achieving superior performance compared to existing methods. An additional reinforcement learning post-training phase enhances the model's ability to produce clinically accurate images, reducing the gap in reliability compared to real scans by 47% according to an independent classifier. Alongside the model, the researchers have released a synthetic dataset of approximately 200,000 chest CT volumes with detailed clinical conditioning metadata. This dataset supports a wide range of clinical findings and offers a valuable resource for further research and development in medical image synthesis and analysis.

item.title: Researchers propose MolBasic framework to improve molecular large language models' structural understanding via bidirectional SMILES-Graph translation and progressive learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MolBasic, a new framework designed to enhance molecular large language models' understanding of molecular structures by focusing on bidirectional translation between SMILES strings and molecular graphs. This approach addresses the limitation of current models that, despite strong performance in molecular tasks, struggle with basic structure recognition, which is crucial since molecular function is determined by structure. MolBasic uses a multi-level structure perception benchmark and a progressive learning scheme to improve alignment between sequential and topological molecular representations. The framework incorporates a standardized Chain-of-Thought method to guide models from learning structural details to performing higher-level molecular reasoning. Experimental results demonstrate that MolBasic significantly improves structural comprehension and leads to better outcomes in downstream applications such as property prediction and molecular optimization, supporting the effectiveness of a structure-first approach in molecular language modeling.

item.title: Researchers propose HyperVAttention, a training-free sparse attention framework using spatio-temporal clustering to improve efficiency and fidelity in video diffusion transformers, reducing latency by up to 2.13× [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced HyperVAttention (HVA), a training-free sparse attention framework designed to enhance efficiency and fidelity in Video Diffusion Transformers (VDiTs) used for high-quality video generation. HVA addresses the limitations of existing clustering-based sparse attention methods by reducing clustering overhead and improving GPU execution efficiency, resulting in up to a 2.13× reduction in latency while maintaining or improving video fidelity. The framework employs 3D local-window clustering to leverage spatio-temporal locality, restricting centroid searches to fixed neighborhoods and implementing this with a custom Triton kernel for speed. It also uses a hybrid clustering strategy that updates only subsets of tokens at intermediate steps, capitalizing on temporal stability. Additionally, hardware-aware cluster merging optimizes GPU block utilization by aligning clusters with execution tiles, enhancing both computational efficiency and approximation accuracy. Experiments on text-to-video generation demonstrate that HVA sets a new standard for training-free sparse attention in video diffusion models, effectively balancing speed and quality. This advancement could enable more practical generation of longer-duration, high-fidelity videos using diffusion transformers.

item.title: Researchers propose OmniFocus, a training-free query-guided token compression method for audio-visual large language models that improves efficiency and maintains accuracy at 25% token retention [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced OmniFocus, a training-free, query-guided token compression method designed for omni-modal large language models (OmniLLMs) that process both audio and video inputs. OmniFocus independently estimates the importance of tokens in each modality, enabling balanced compression that preserves key information from both audio and video while maintaining their alignment. This approach addresses limitations of previous methods that relied on unimodal guidance and assumed temporal alignment of information density across modalities. Tests on the Qwen2.5-Omni model family across multiple audio-visual benchmarks demonstrate that OmniFocus achieves strong performance even when retaining only 25% of tokens. For instance, on the DailyOmni benchmark with Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, it maintains 59.40% accuracy and offers up to a 1.38 times speedup in inference compared to using all tokens, highlighting an effective balance between accuracy and computational efficiency.

item.title: Researchers propose LACE-SVD, a loss-aware SVD method with cumulative error correction for LLM compression, improving LLaMA-7B performance at high compression ratios [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced LACE-SVD, a novel loss-aware singular value decomposition (SVD) method designed to improve compression of large language models (LLMs) like LLaMA-7B. This approach addresses key limitations of existing SVD-based compression techniques by considering layer-wise loss sensitivity and correcting cumulative errors that propagate through the model's residual stream. LACE-SVD optimizes rank allocation under compression constraints and applies local updates alongside propagation-aware corrections to reduce discrepancies in layer outputs. Experimental results demonstrate that LACE-SVD significantly outperforms previous methods such as Dobi-SVD, achieving a lower perplexity on the WikiText-2 benchmark at a high compression ratio of 0.6. This advancement offers a more effective way to reduce memory and computational demands of large models without sacrificing performance, supporting more efficient deployment of LLMs across diverse hardware platforms.

item.title: Researchers propose Subspace-Aligned Rewiring (SAR) to extract reasoning-effective updates from large language models' spectral space, improving reasoning, multi-domain training, and model merging with under 1% of parameters [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Subspace-Aligned Rewiring (SAR), a method that improves large language models by extracting reasoning-effective updates concentrated in the model's spectral space. SAR retains these core updates while removing orthogonal components that can suppress reasoning performance or cause interference during multi-domain training and model merging. This approach uses less than 1% of the model's parameters to preserve over 99% of post-training performance and enhances capabilities in mathematical reasoning and coding tasks. SAR has demonstrated effectiveness across various model families and scales, improving exploration in mathematical reasoning and generalizing to agentic coding benchmarks. It also purifies mixed-domain training updates by restoring suppressed coding abilities without compromising other skills. Additionally, SAR facilitates model merging across different expert domains, achieving better cross-domain generalization than previous methods and outperforming single-domain experts. Overall, SAR offers a training-free technique to enhance reasoning and multi-domain performance by leveraging the geometry of parameter updates, addressing key deployment challenges in large language models such as performance saturation and capability interference.

item.title: Researchers propose PixCon, a clean-positive pixel-contrastive learning framework for foundation-model semi-supervised segmentation that guarantees contamination-free positive sets and improves accuracy on Pascal VOC, Cityscapes, and ADE20K [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced PixCon, a clean-positive pixel-contrastive learning framework designed for semi-supervised semantic segmentation using foundation models. PixCon ensures contamination-free positive sets by maintaining a per-class memory bank that only includes correctly classified labeled pixels, improving accuracy without adding inference-time parameters or requiring threshold tuning. This approach outperforms or matches strong baselines on datasets like Pascal VOC, Cityscapes, and ADE20K. The framework leverages a DINOv2 teacher model to generate highly clean pseudo-labels and addresses the issue of contamination in contrastive learning by eliminating false positives in the positive set. Analysis shows that contamination negatively impacts learning, and PixCon's design guarantees zero contamination, enhancing robustness especially as teacher model quality varies. The method achieves consistent improvements in mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) scores, demonstrating its effectiveness as a low-cost, reliable solution for foundation-model semi-supervised segmentation.

item.title: Researchers present STELLA, an efficient sensor-to-LLM translation framework for on-device human activity recognition achieving up to 11.83% F1 improvement and real-time inference on edge devices [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed STELLA, a new framework that enables efficient on-device human activity recognition (HAR) by translating sensor data into inputs for large language models (LLMs). STELLA uses a lightweight hierarchical tokenizer to compress multi-channel sensor data into compact tokens, which are then processed by a frozen pretrained LLM combined with natural-language prompts for accurate activity classification. This approach reduces the need for extensive LLM adaptation, supports on-device personalization, and maintains privacy by keeping all data and inference local to the device. STELLA was tested across seven public HAR datasets and eight benchmark settings, achieving up to an 11.83% improvement in F1 score over previous methods. Personalization on the device further improved performance by up to 21.91% as user-specific data accumulated. The framework also outperformed other time-series tokenizers within the same LLM pipeline and demonstrated real-time inference capabilities on mobile and edge devices, highlighting its potential for practical, private, and personalized HAR applications on resource-constrained hardware.

item.title: Researchers propose Proactive Thinking framework for large language models to pre-compute responses during conversational downtime, improving dialogue efficiency without performance loss [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a Proactive Thinking framework for large language models (LLMs) that enables these models to pre-compute potential responses during conversational downtime, rather than waiting passively for user input. This approach aims to reduce latency and improve the fluidity of dialogue by allowing the model to anticipate and prepare future content, similar to how humans plan during natural pauses in conversation. The framework includes a training-free baseline that balances efficiency and quality through speculative continual thinking. To test this method, the researchers adapted three benchmarks into time-aware environments that simulate real-time conversational flow. Their results show that proactive thinking enhances interaction efficiency without sacrificing performance, suggesting a shift toward more intelligent and anticipatory conversational AI systems that operate in real time.

item.title: Researchers propose Adaptive Credit Policy Optimization (ACPO) using fine-grained surrogate entropy for token-level credit assignment in reinforcement learning, improving performance on reasoning and coding benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Adaptive Credit Policy Optimization (ACPO), a new framework for token-level credit assignment in reinforcement learning (RL) aimed at improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). ACPO uses a fine-grained surrogate entropy to modulate policy updates, focusing on uncertain decisions in successful outcomes and overconfident tokens in failures, addressing challenges posed by sparse outcome rewards and limitations of existing methods. The approach provides deterministic entropy bounds and maintains alignment with policy-gradient directions under certain conditions. Experimental results on mathematical reasoning and coding benchmarks, including AIME 2025 and HumanEvalPro, demonstrate that ACPO consistently outperforms established RL baselines such as DAPO, GTPO, and SAPO, highlighting its potential to enhance token-level learning in complex tasks.

item.title: Researchers introduce CuBAS, a curvature-based adaptive sampling method for supervised classification that improves training set informativeness using geometric complexity across 60+ benchmark datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CuBAS (Curvature-Based Adaptive Sampling), a novel method for supervised classification that enhances the informativeness of training sets by leveraging the geometric complexity of data distributions. CuBAS models labeled datasets as statistical manifolds and uses local curvature, derived from Fisher information, to identify regions of varying complexity. This approach partitions data into low-curvature clusters and high-curvature decision boundaries, enabling the selection of compact, highly informative training subsets. The method constructs a k-nearest-neighbor graph and computes curvature scores using the Potts Markov random field model, allowing efficient and interpretable sampling. Evaluations on over 60 benchmark datasets show that CuBAS consistently outperforms random and uncertainty-based sampling strategies across different labeling budgets and classifier types. CuBAS is computationally efficient and grounded in differential geometry, offering a theoretically sound and practical tool for improving supervised learning.

item.title: Researchers propose Threshold Gating as a universal primitive for neural network nonlinearity, demonstrating equivalence to standard activations and enabling efficient training and hardware implementation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Threshold Gating (TG) as a universal primitive for neural network nonlinearity, demonstrating that common activation functions like ReLU, Sigmoid, and Softmax can be represented as instances of TG. This approach preserves model performance across various architectures, including CNNs, transformers, and recurrent networks, without requiring retraining. TG also supports training from scratch, offering improvements in model compression, performance, and training efficiency. The study further proposes a 'Minimal Branch Theorem' linking the number of TG branches to neural network trainability. Additionally, TG facilitates a unified hardware implementation for analog in-memory systems, potentially reducing power consumption and chip area by addressing bottlenecks associated with analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters.

item.title: Researchers propose DMKGC, a conditional diffusion-guided framework for multi-domain knowledge graph completion, improving tail entity prediction by 4.3% MRR across 14 KGs and 3 benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced DMKGC, a novel conditional diffusion-guided framework designed to enhance multi-domain knowledge graph completion (MKGC). This approach improves the prediction of missing triples in a target knowledge graph by transferring knowledge from multiple support graphs without compromising domain-specific information. DMKGC treats each knowledge graph as a partial view of an entity's full information and generates domain-general embeddings through diffusion models conditioned on support graphs, achieving a 4.3% average improvement in mean reciprocal rank (MRR) for tail entity prediction across 14 knowledge graphs and three benchmarks. The framework initializes domain-agnostic entity embeddings and encodes them within individual graphs before fusing equivalent entities from support graphs to guide the diffusion process. This method ensures unbiased generation of embeddings while preserving domain-specific characteristics, addressing limitations of previous approaches that enforced strict consistency constraints and risked losing contextual information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DMKGC maintains performance gains even in low-resource data scenarios, highlighting its effectiveness in knowledge transfer across diverse domains.

item.title: Study compares algorithm specification formats for language models implementing machine learning tasks, finding LaTeX pseudocode most effective under core information settings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study published on arXiv investigates how different algorithm specification formats affect the accuracy of large language models (LLMs) when implementing machine learning algorithms. The research compares formats including ordinary prose, LaTeX pseudocode, Markdown, YAML, JSON, and Python code stubs across multiple tasks and models, analyzing 4,020 generated implementations. The findings reveal that LaTeX algorithm-style pseudocode yields the highest accuracy under core information conditions, while YAML and prose formats also perform well; code stubs do not consistently improve correctness despite defining function signatures. The study evaluates critical implementation details such as tie-breaking, array shapes, numerical rules, return structures, and handling of invalid inputs. Under complete information settings, some models like GPT-5.4 mini show no significant differences between formats, whereas others still do. The results suggest that authors should explicitly specify interfaces, computation steps, numerical rules, and boundary-case behaviors rather than relying on the format alone to convey these details.

item.title: Study examines GPT-5.2 Spanish-Chinese journalistic translation quality under 48 prompt conditions, finding translation theory-driven prompts reduce awkward style errors but prompt language has minimal impact [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study investigated the impact of prompt language and translation theory-driven prompt design on the quality of Spanish-Chinese journalistic translations produced by GPT-5.2. Using a parallel corpus of four editorials from El Pais, translations were generated under 48 different conditions varying prompt types and languages. Evaluation through automated metrics and human assessment revealed that while automated measures favored a baseline prompt, human evaluators preferred a brief-oriented prompt, highlighting differences in evaluation methods. The study found that prompts informed by translation theory helped reduce awkward style errors, though unidiomatic expressions remained common, and the language of the prompt had little effect on translation quality. These findings suggest that incorporating translation theory into prompt design can enhance translation quality in expert evaluations, particularly for journalistic texts. However, the study notes that the educational benefits of such prompts for language learners are still uncertain and require further research involving user-based studies to validate their effectiveness.

item.title: Researchers analyze decentralised federated learning over temporal networks, finding structural and temporal heterogeneities slow convergence compared to typical experimental scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have examined decentralised federated learning, a peer-to-peer approach for on-device machine learning model training that enhances privacy and communication efficiency without a single point of failure. Their study reveals that structural and temporal heterogeneities in communication networks significantly slow the convergence of the learning process compared to typical experimental setups, which often overlook these factors. The learning dynamics correspond to a lazy random-walk diffusion on temporal networks, highlighting the impact of real-world network irregularities on training speed. By analyzing real-world temporal networks, the researchers found that these inhomogeneities commonly cause a marked slowdown in diffusion and thus in the convergence of the federated learning process. This insight challenges the optimistic convergence rates reported in many experimental scenarios and underscores the need to consider network heterogeneity for more accurate assessments of decentralised federated learning performance.
