item.title: Researchers introduce CRRL, a causality-based reinforcement learning framework that trains autonomous system policies to collaborate with rule-based recovery, improving navigation and reducing stalled states in driving scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CRRL, a causality-based reinforcement learning framework designed to improve autonomous system recovery by training policies that effectively collaborate with rule-based recovery mechanisms. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning, which often stalls in failure states and struggles to generalize to new scenarios, by incorporating causal relations from driving logs to help the system anticipate and respond to stalled states. CRRL integrates sensor data collection, causal model construction, and hybrid policy training to enhance navigation performance and reduce immobilization during driving tasks. Evaluated through a comprehensive ablation study across multiple driving scenarios, CRRL demonstrated significant improvements in reward, distance traveled, and velocity compared to conventional methods. Notably, in roundabout navigation tests, nearly half of the episodes required no recovery intervention, indicating the framework's effectiveness in producing robust policies that cooperate seamlessly with rule-based safety components. These findings suggest that causal-guided training can enhance the reliability and adaptability of autonomous driving systems.

item.title: Researchers develop ParMaxFEM, a parallelized C++ implementation of MaxFEM for scalable maximal frequent episode mining integrated into Desbordante, achieving up to 35× speedup on 8 cores
item.description: Researchers have developed ParMaxFEM, a parallelized C++ implementation of the MaxFEM algorithm for maximal frequent episode mining, integrated into the open-source data profiler Desbordante. This new approach addresses the computational challenges of mining frequently appearing subsequences by improving performance and scalability, achieving up to an 8× speedup over the original SPMF implementation and up to 35× speedup using 8-core parallelization. ParMaxFEM enhances the original MaxFEM by applying efficient pruning techniques and parallel processing, enabling faster discovery of maximal frequent episodes in event sequences. The integration with Desbordante allows users to treat patterns as first-class entities and supports custom program development for pattern discovery and validation, making the tool more accessible and versatile for data analysis tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose a Bayesian framework using conditional variational autoencoders to evaluate scenario compatibility and structural uncertainty in generative population synthesis for transportation planning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a Bayesian framework using conditional variational autoencoders to assess the compatibility of scenario targets with generative population synthesis models in transportation planning. This approach quantifies how well future aggregate population assumptions align with the structural patterns learned by generative models, addressing uncertainties that arise when imposing scenario constraints. The framework uses an ensemble of population realizations and Bayesian updating to measure scenario feasibility and the impact on structural uncertainty. The method involves training a population-aware conditional variational autoencoder to capture plausible population structures while maintaining aggregate accuracy. Scenario targets are incorporated as probabilistic evidence, and their compatibility is evaluated through effective sample size metrics that reflect the concentration of posterior distributions. Experiments show that scenario effects depend on both the magnitude of targets and their alignment with the model's learned structure, revealing potential failures when targets fall outside the model's support. This probabilistic diagnostic tool offers transportation planners a way to evaluate the feasibility and structural consistency of scenarios before proceeding with projections and planning, potentially improving the reliability of scenario-based analyses in transportation systems.

item.title: Researchers develop a vision-language agent for self-specializing calibration of superconducting transmon chips using a physics-grounded simulation environment and gradient-free online adaptation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a vision-language agent designed to autonomously calibrate superconducting transmon chips by integrating a physics-grounded simulation environment with gradient-free online adaptation. This agent sequentially selects experiments, interprets ambiguous data, and updates its calibration strategy without weight updates, effectively managing noise, drift, and limited experimental budgets. The approach includes a realistic simulation of chip behavior, an agent that processes visual and textual information to maintain calibration, and an adaptation mechanism that refines performance based on past anomalies. Testing on challenging chips demonstrated significant improvements in gate fidelity and reduced variance, with the agent successfully diagnosing hardware faults without direct access to ground truth. The system's scoring and reward mechanisms are transferable to real hardware, indicating potential for practical deployment in quantum device calibration.

item.title: OpenGlass introduces a local-first, privacy-focused split architecture for real-time visual assistance using ESP32 glasses and nearby device MLLM inference, targeting blind and low-vision users [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenGlass is an open-source system designed to provide real-time visual assistance with a focus on privacy and low latency, primarily benefiting blind and low-vision users. It uses a split architecture where an ESP32-based unit on wearable glasses captures visual data, while a nearby consumer device performs local multimodal large language model (MLLM) inference and speech output. This approach minimizes reliance on cloud services, keeping sensitive visual data on user-controlled devices and reducing network delays. The system achieves median user-to-audio response times under two seconds in most trials, supporting tasks such as obstacle awareness, sign and object queries, and image quality checks. OpenGlass is intended as a reference platform rather than a certified navigation aid, and its developers have released the source code, hardware instructions, prompts, evaluation data, and logs to encourage further research and development in privacy-focused assistive technologies.

item.title: Researchers propose unbiased alignment methods for large language models using Unbiased Reward Model and Direct Preference Optimization losses to handle noisy human preference data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed new methods to improve the alignment of large language models with human preferences by addressing the issue of noisy data in preference datasets. They introduced the Unbiased Reward Model (URM) loss and the Unbiased Direct Preference Optimization (UDPO) loss, which mathematically correct distortions caused by noise, enabling unbiased training without the need for clean ground-truth data. These approaches have been theoretically validated for noise tolerance and compatibility, and experimental results show they outperform existing state-of-the-art methods across various datasets. The proposed framework offers a robust solution to the challenges posed by real-world noisy preference data, which commonly affects reinforcement learning from human feedback and direct preference optimization techniques. By providing rigorous theoretical analysis and practical code availability, this work advances the reliability and effectiveness of aligning language models with human values and preferences.

item.title: Researchers release WorldTensor, a harmonised global dataset integrating environmental and socioeconomic data on a 0.25° grid for Earth system foundation model training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed WorldTensor, a harmonised global dataset that integrates hundreds of environmental and socioeconomic variables onto a standardized 0.25° spatial grid with an annual temporal framework. This dataset combines diverse data sources including climate, land, ocean, cryosphere, infrastructure, hazards, and socioeconomic indicators, addressing the lack of unified training resources for Earth system foundation models that consider both physical and human systems. WorldTensor was created by regridding inputs from various resolutions and projections, converting point and vector data into gridded fields, and aligning temporal coverages from daily to multiyear observations. The dataset is distributed as NetCDF files with standardized metadata, providing a reproducible resource designed to support machine learning workflows for training and evaluating models that capture coupled dynamics across environmental and human systems at a planetary scale.

item.title: Researchers present an automated pipeline using DeepSeek V3 to extract structured legal reasoning and control citation hallucinations in 330,000 Italian tax-court judgments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an automated pipeline that breaks down approximately 330,000 Italian tax-court judgments into individual legal issues and extracts structured XML representations based on the IRAC framework and legal syllogism. This system uses the DeepSeek V3 model to efficiently process the large corpus while incorporating a hallucination-detection filter to verify legal citations against a dedicated parser, ensuring accuracy in referencing. The pipeline was validated on 50 judgments annotated by tax law experts, demonstrating strong agreement between the model and human annotators in issue extraction and citation accuracy. This approach represents the first expert-validated, issue-level structured extraction system with hallucination control for Italian tax-court decisions, enabling applications such as issue-level retrieval, citation-network analysis, and the creation of extensive datasets for legal reasoning research.

item.title: Researchers present SPORK, a training-free controller that accelerates agentic LLM inference by speculatively forking tool calls, reducing Qwen3-32B's GAIA P95 latency by 18% without accuracy loss [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SPORK, a training-free controller designed to accelerate inference in agentic large language models (LLMs) by speculatively forking tool calls. This approach reduces the latency of Qwen3-32B's GAIA P95 by 18% without compromising accuracy. SPORK works by predicting upcoming tool calls early in the generation process, allowing tool execution to overlap with ongoing reasoning, thereby minimizing idle GPU time. SPORK leverages the model itself as a predictor, achieving high accuracy in forecasting tool usage across multiple benchmarks. It incorporates a cost model and mechanisms such as prefix-cache forks, confidence gates, and partial-token acceptance to optimize speculation and handle mispredictions gracefully. The system falls back to serial execution if speculation fails, ensuring correctness is maintained. The method is effective across various model sizes and architectures, including dense and mixture-of-experts models, and maintains task accuracy within one percentage point of baseline performance. SPORK operates as a lightweight controller over standard completion APIs without requiring retraining or auxiliary models, making it suitable for immediate deployment. The project is open source and available for use and further development.

item.title: Researchers present FedAvg algorithm results for Human Activity Recognition, analyzing trade-offs between personalized and generalized accuracy under varying client data conditions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have evaluated the FedAvg algorithm within the Human Activity Recognition (HAR) domain to explore the balance between personalized and generalized model accuracy in federated learning. Their study compares centralized, local, and federated learning approaches, including scenarios simulating changes in client data distribution. The results indicate that while FedAvg generally offers improved personalization alongside strong generalization compared to traditional centralized learning, this advantage diminishes under challenging conditions such as varying class distributions across clients. The research involved designing multiple testing scenarios to assess performance trade-offs, highlighting the complexities of maintaining both personalization and generalization in federated learning environments. These findings underscore the need for careful consideration of client data variability when deploying federated learning models in real-world applications.

item.title: Researchers propose PedestrianDiffusion, a multimodal generative denoising framework for dense 6D inertial navigation state estimation with state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced PedestrianDiffusion, a novel multimodal generative framework designed to improve dense 6D inertial navigation state estimation. This approach addresses the limitations of consumer-grade inertial navigation caused by noise in Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) by reformulating state estimation as a continuous conditional denoising process in the frequency domain. The method incorporates a zero-shot semantic conditioning mechanism using vision-language embeddings to adapt to diverse sensor noise profiles and employs a single-step deterministic solver to enable efficient asynchronous batch trajectory refinement on edge devices. Extensive testing on multiple benchmarks, including OxIOD, RIDI, RoNIN, and TLIO, demonstrates that PedestrianDiffusion achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness against impulse disturbances and kinematic drift. This work offers a comprehensive algorithmic foundation for the development of next-generation Neural Inertial Measurement Units (N-IMUs), potentially advancing the performance and reliability of inertial navigation systems in consumer applications.

item.title: Researchers propose spectral shape-based metrics to manage and quantify large language models using weight empirical spectral density, enabling lineage tracking and performance analysis across diverse open-source LLMs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced spectral shape-based metrics to manage and quantify large language models (LLMs) by analyzing the empirical spectral density of model weights. This approach, grounded in Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization theory, provides a compact spectral signature that captures intrinsic properties of pretrained models and remains stable after training, facilitating model-level analysis without relying on task-specific benchmarks. The method is data-free, computationally efficient, and scale-invariant, making it suitable for large-scale evaluation across diverse LLM architectures and training procedures. The team compiled a comprehensive corpus of major open-source LLM families to benchmark spectral and non-spectral metrics across various models and downstream tasks. Their findings demonstrate that the spectral signature can effectively track model lineage, cluster similar models without supervision, and serve as a proxy for assessing model performance. This metric offers a practical tool for organizing, comparing, and analyzing extensive collections of LLMs, addressing challenges in model management, licensing, and evaluation.

item.title: Researchers introduce Amortised Sequential Information Gathering to fine-tune LLMs with Bayesian Experimental Design, doubling 7B model success on 20 Questions and cutting inference cost 25x [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Amortised Sequential Information Gathering (ASIG), a fine-tuning method that integrates Bayesian Experimental Design into large language model (LLM) policies to improve sequential information gathering. Tested on the 20 Questions task, ASIG more than doubled the success rate of a 7-billion-parameter model while reducing inference costs by over 25 times compared to a leading baseline. The approach also enhanced performance on MediQ, a medical diagnosis benchmark not seen during training, indicating its ability to generalize to new domains. ASIG achieves these improvements by extending Group Relative Policy Optimisation with an Expected Information Gain reward, enabling LLMs to gather information more effectively across multi-turn interactions. This method offers a computationally efficient way to fine-tune LLMs for sequential decision-making tasks, demonstrating promising transferability and practical benefits in information-seeking applications.

item.title: Researchers introduce Agentic Test-Time Training to reduce performance drift in LLM agents during long episodes, improving success rates by up to 5 points on ALFWorld and SWE-bench Lite [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Agentic Test-Time Training (aTTT), a method designed to reduce performance degradation in large language model (LLM) agents during extended task episodes. LLM agents often struggle over long interactions by revisiting states, repeating failed actions, and losing effective strategies. aTTT addresses this by continuously adapting model weights with a token-level reweighting technique that downplays repeated tokens from prior updates while fully weighting novel tokens, thereby mitigating drift caused by repetitive training data. The team implemented a concurrent serving system using vLLM's runtime LoRA API to enable live updates with minimal overhead. Testing on benchmarks like ALFWorld and SWE-bench Lite showed that aTTT improved success rates by up to 5 points, particularly preserving existing task competence over long trajectories rather than teaching new skills. This approach offers a promising way to maintain LLM agent performance in complex, multi-turn environments.

item.title: Researchers introduce TRIAGE, a stage-aware instrumentation framework for evaluating automated knowledge graphs in document-grounded graph retrieval-augmented generation with interpretable metrics across extraction, validation, and usage stages [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TRIAGE, a stage-aware instrumentation framework designed to evaluate automated knowledge graphs used in document-grounded graph retrieval-augmented generation (Graph-RAG). TRIAGE provides interpretable metrics across three key stages-knowledge graph implementation, expert validation, and usage-to assess the trustworthiness and query cost of the underlying graph. This framework enables precise localization of failures within the extraction, graph construction, or retrieval phases, improving diagnostic accuracy beyond simply identifying incorrect final answers. The framework attaches specific metrics such as triple confidence, source coverage, and schema checks during implementation; structural quality assessments during expert validation; and retrieval coverage, faithfulness, and cost during usage. Most metrics operate without requiring gold-standard annotations, which are only used for offline calibration when references are available. TRIAGE forms a diagnostic chain that identifies the earliest stage where a failure occurs, guiding targeted remediation efforts. As a theoretical framework, TRIAGE includes a proof of concept and a reproducible evaluation protocol, offering a systematic approach to improve the reliability and interpretability of automatically constructed knowledge graphs in AI-driven retrieval systems.

item.title: Researchers propose SkillOpt-Lite, a minimal pipeline for autonomous agent skill optimization that accelerates convergence and outperforms prior methods, integrated into VSCode Copilot for one-line skill evolution [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced SkillOpt-Lite, a streamlined pipeline for optimizing autonomous agent skills that simplifies existing complex methods while ensuring theoretical and empirical rigor. This approach formalizes skill optimization through Zeroth-Order optimization and incorporates principles such as file-system-based trajectory exploration, consensus attribute mining, and independent validation gating to enhance convergence and generalization. SkillOpt-Lite demonstrates improved performance, notably boosting LiveMath scores on GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4-nano models, with the latter surpassing standard GPT-5.4 optimized by previous methods. The framework has been integrated into production coding tools like VSCode Copilot, allowing developers to evolve agent skills with minimal effort through a single line of code. By treating all agent components as editable code, SkillOpt-Lite naturally extends to full harness optimization, further improving accuracy on benchmarks such as SpreadsheetBench. The researchers have made the code publicly available to support further development and adoption.

item.title: Researchers propose Best-of-Better-N, an in-context learning framework that improves response alignment by retrieving and restyling high-reward examples for large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Best-of-Better-N (BoBN), an in-context learning framework designed to enhance response alignment in large language models by retrieving and restyling high-reward examples relevant to the input query. This method addresses limitations of existing inference-time alignment techniques, such as Best-of-N, which struggle when the reference model assigns low probability to high-quality responses. BoBN uses a restyling step where retrieved responses are rewritten to match the target task's format and style, effectively shifting the model's output distribution toward higher-reward responses. The team analytically demonstrates how in-context learning with BoBN provably improves alignment on target tasks. They evaluated the approach on safety alignment and mathematical reasoning benchmarks across multiple reference language models, finding that BoBN achieves better performance with a fixed number of responses and requires fewer samples to reach target performance levels. This advancement offers a promising alternative to training-based alignment methods by improving the quality and relevance of generated outputs through retrieval and restyling.

item.title: Researchers propose a comprehensive benchmarking framework for mutual information estimation using copula-theoretic tests and evaluate non-parametric, discriminative, and generative estimators on complex data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a comprehensive benchmarking framework for mutual information (MI) estimation, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks that focus on simplified, low-dimensional data. Their approach uses a unified copula-theoretic perspective and introduces two families of tests that vary MI, dimensionality, and marginal complexity with synthetic and real-world data. They evaluated non-parametric, discriminative, and generative MI estimators, finding that no single method consistently outperforms others across all scenarios. The framework includes a copula-first family of tests that systematically adjusts ground-truth MI and data complexity, and a marginals-first family that integrates real image data with controlled dependency structures. This extensive evaluation revealed fundamental challenges in MI estimation and led to the proposal of new tests targeting these limitations. The researchers have made their benchmarking code openly available to support further study and development in this area.

item.title: Researchers introduce PULS, a semantic world-model pipeline with KSD Bridge and Anticipatory State Predictor, achieving high video anomaly anticipation accuracy and zero-shot transfer on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PULS (Predictive Unified Latent Space), a semantic world-model pipeline designed for continuous video anomaly anticipation. PULS integrates two key components: the KSD Bridge, which translates physical motion data into a semantic embedding space, and the Anticipatory State Predictor (ASP), which refines predicted future states. This approach achieves high accuracy in detecting anomalies on the UCF-Crime dataset and demonstrates strong zero-shot transfer performance on the out-of-distribution XD-Violence dataset without relying on traditional Multiple Instance Learning methods. The KSD Bridge maps physical tensors into a text-aligned semantic space, enabling chunk-level anomaly detection with AUROC scores of 0.8994 for UCF-Crime and 0.8162 for XD-Violence. The researchers propose the Latent Clarity Hypothesis, suggesting that anticipated future representations are more semantically distinct than observed data due to the model's ability to filter out noise while preserving motion information. The ASP enhances these future representations, significantly improving zero-shot video question answering accuracy compared to baselines. This work separates anticipation from observation by showing that predicted future states occupy distinct semantic subspaces, validated through a novel Triple-Track Lead-Time protocol. The findings indicate that Newtonian-invariant kinematic representations generalize well across datasets, highlighting the potential of PULS for robust, anticipatory video anomaly detection in diverse environments.

item.title: Researchers propose knowledge distillation framework focusing on teacher representation equivalence classes rather than absolute features, validated on Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.1 models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a new framework for knowledge distillation that focuses on teaching a student model the equivalence class of a teacher's representation rather than its absolute features. This approach addresses the issue that pretrained representations are only identifiable up to orthogonal and isotropic scaling transformations, making absolute feature matching ill-posed. The framework unifies various distillation methods by targeting class invariants such as Gram structure and principal subspaces, and it has been validated on the Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.1 models. The study includes a restoration experiment showing that while a corrupted model's representation can be nearly recovered, its capability cannot, highlighting that output-function (logit) matching is crucial for restoring capability. Additionally, a grafting experiment demonstrated that overlap in representation boundaries predicts successful transplantation of model components, though it is not sufficient on its own. These findings emphasize the importance of aligning output functions over hidden features for effective knowledge transfer.

item.title: Researchers present Native Differentiable Virtual Machine for neuro-symbolic learning, enabling efficient runtime differentiation of executable programs with 24x faster high-quality solutions in LLM co-search [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Native Differentiable Virtual Machine (NDVM), a runtime system that enables efficient differentiation of executable programs without compiling each candidate into separate graphs. This approach separates symbolic program structure from differentiable numeric state, allowing gradient-based optimization to be amortized across many parameter vectors. NDVM achieves significant speedups, reaching high-quality solutions about 24 times faster in co-search tasks involving large language model (LLM) proposed programs. NDVM maintains native runtime data for symbolic elements while storing numeric payloads in dense batched buffers with exact reverse-mode gradients recorded along execution traces. This design overcomes the limitations of previous methods that either sacrificed program-as-data flexibility or incurred heavy interpreter overhead. Implemented as a native runtime with near-linear multicore scaling and multiple front ends, NDVM offers a practical foundation for scientific discovery workflows that require joint program and parameter optimization.

item.title: Researchers introduce RADIO1D, a variable-length 1D token sequence for vision-language models that compresses images with multi-teacher distillation, enabling efficient scene understanding and improved image retrieval [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed RADIO1D, a novel approach for vision-language models that compresses images into a compact, variable-length one-dimensional token sequence. This method challenges the traditional reliance on fixed patch-based two-dimensional vision features by leveraging multi-teacher knowledge distillation and an autoencoder design to create hierarchical, abstract representations that summarize global image content effectively. RADIO1D enables accurate scene understanding even with minimal tokens and supports enhanced composition-aware image retrieval. The study found that during vision-language model training, vision encoders produce increasingly abstract and less spatially coherent features, with some models developing specialized tokens that capture essential image information. RADIO1D builds on this insight by offering flexible accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs through adjustable token counts, achieving competitive performance across various multimodal benchmarks while reducing computational overhead and improving accuracy compared to existing methods.

item.title: Researchers propose Trimodal Coherent Co-attention Transformer using optical and PolInSAR data for tropical forest biomass estimation, achieving under 5% error in dense Amazon regions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Trimodal Coherent Co-attention Transformer (TCCT), a deep learning model that integrates optical data from Landsat-5 with complex-valued Polarimetric SAR Interferometry (PolInSAR) data to improve Above-Ground Biomass (AGB) estimation in dense tropical forests. This approach addresses challenges like SAR signal saturation and cloud cover by preserving spatial phase coherence and dynamically weighting data sources, achieving less than 5% relative error in biomass estimates for dense Amazon regions. The TCCT model was fine-tuned using localized calibration specific to the Paracou region in the Amazon basin and evaluated through rigorous cross-validation and spatial fine-tuning. It outperformed traditional methods such as Random Forest, CNN, and Vision Transformer models in canopy height prediction and biomass estimation, meeting the European Space Agency's BIOMASS mission accuracy requirements. This advancement offers a robust framework for continuous carbon stock monitoring in tropical biomes, potentially enhancing remote sensing capabilities for forest biomass assessment and contributing to climate change mitigation efforts.

item.title: Researchers conduct first controlled longitudinal study isolating scaffolding impact on coding agent quality, analyzing 35 Qwen Code CLI releases with fixed LLM [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers conducted the first controlled longitudinal study to isolate the impact of scaffolding-the middleware layer between developers and large language models (LLMs)-on the quality of coding agents. By fixing the underlying LLM and varying only the scaffolding across 35 sequential releases of the Qwen Code CLI, they evaluated agent effectiveness and efficiency on software engineering tasks, revealing how scaffolding evolution influences performance independently of the model itself. The study analyzed rapid development cycles of five major open-source scaffoldings, noting release frequencies exceeding two per day and thousands of issues addressed within months. Detailed evaluation linked quality fluctuations to specific development patterns and architectural components, supported by qualitative evidence connecting individual code changes to measured shifts in agent quality. These findings challenge the common assumption that regressions in coding agent performance stem solely from the underlying LLM, highlighting the significant role of scaffolding evolution. This insight may guide future development and maintenance practices to improve the reliability and effectiveness of autonomous coding systems.

item.title: Researchers release a failure-mode benchmark and evaluation framework for polymorphic sybil poisoning attacks in retrieval-augmented generation, revealing a 5.7× amplification in hijack attacks and unmonitored failure profiles across multiple readers [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a new benchmark and evaluation framework to assess failure modes in grounded question answering systems under coordinated retrieval poisoning attacks. Their framework categorizes reader outputs into four distinct types-gold, hijack, abstention, and drift-and employs a Forced Exposure protocol to separate reader conflict resolution from retrieval variability. They also identify a novel attack method called polymorphic sybil poisoning, where multiple lexically diverse passages support a malicious target while evading detection by near-duplicate filters, resulting in a 5.7-fold increase in hijack attacks compared to monomorphic baselines. The study reveals that traditional metrics like ASR fail to capture significant portions of attack-induced failures, such as abstention and drift, which together account for 47-66% of outputs and vary notably between readers. The researchers provide a comprehensive benchmark dataset, evaluation tools, and testing protocols across multiple readers and datasets, making these resources publicly available under open licenses to support further research and defense development against such sophisticated poisoning attacks.

item.title: Researchers propose EmCom-Diffusion, a framework using fine-tuned text-to-image diffusion models to directly measure visual reflection in emergent languages by reconstructing input images from emergent messages [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced EmCom-Diffusion, a novel framework designed to directly measure visual reflection in emergent languages by reconstructing input images from their corresponding emergent messages. This approach fine-tunes a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model on pairs of images and emergent messages, evaluating the similarity between the reconstructed and original images to assess how well the messages preserve visual information without relying on human-defined targets or the original speaker-listener pair. The framework was tested using the MS-COCO dataset within a Referential Game setting and validated against various baselines and existing metrics, including CBM, supervised translation, TopSim, and R@1. EmCom-Diffusion demonstrated an improved ability to capture visual content encoded in emergent languages that other metrics often miss, offering a more direct and generative method for evaluating the visual fidelity of emergent communication systems.

item.title: Researchers propose FedACT, a federated adaptive coordinate trust modulation method to improve Transformer training robustness under data heterogeneity, showing gains in vision Transformers, CNNs, and LLMs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced FedACT, a federated adaptive coordinate trust modulation method designed to enhance the robustness of Transformer training under data heterogeneity. FedACT improves upon existing federated adaptive optimizers by adjusting update magnitudes at the coordinate level based on a trust score, rather than applying uniform corrections across all coordinates. This approach reallocates larger update steps to coordinates supported by both local gradients and global corrections, while maintaining smaller updates on others. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedACT consistently outperforms strong federated adaptive baselines across various models, including vision Transformers, CNNs, and large language models (LLMs) during both pre-training and fine-tuning. The method shows the greatest improvements in Transformer models facing stronger data heterogeneity. Analysis indicates that FedACT enhances cross-client direction consistency, suggesting that coordinate-level trust modulation effectively complements global-local correction mechanisms. The researchers plan to release the code for this method.

item.title: Researchers propose MiPO to fine-tune diffusion classifiers with minority preference optimization, improving zero-shot classification in underrepresented data regions using only caption data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified that diffusion classifiers, while effective in zero-shot classification, tend to perform poorly in minority, low-density regions of data due to biases in pretraining data distribution. To address this, they propose a method called Minority Preference Optimization (MiPO) that fine-tunes pretrained diffusion models by rewarding samples that better represent underrepresented data regions, using only caption data without requiring additional images or external models. This approach enhances minority sampling, broadening coverage of low-density areas and improving classification accuracy in these regions. MiPO operates by generating candidate samples from arbitrary captions, evaluating their coverage of minority regions, and optimizing the model with techniques like LoRA and Group Relative Policy Optimization. The method enables stable and prompt-adaptive minority sampling, effectively translating improved generative coverage into better zero-shot diffusion classification. The researchers demonstrate that diffusion classifiers' perception bias toward majority regions can be mitigated through this optimization and validate MiPO's performance across five standard datasets.

item.title: Researchers develop order-equivariant neural networks unifying graph and sheaf models with universal approximation theorems, extending geometric deep learning symmetry frameworks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed order-equivariant neural networks (OENN) that extend geometric deep learning by incorporating richer symmetry structures. These networks generalize existing graph message passing and sheaf neural networks through the theory of equivariant bundles over face posets. The team characterized all linear order-equivariant maps, constructed OENN layers, and proved universal approximation theorems (UATs) for continuous order-equivariant maps, marking new theoretical advances even for sheaf neural networks where no UAT was previously known. The framework unifies and extends prior models by subsuming sheaf neural networks and broadening the scope of universal approximation results beyond traditional graph neural networks. Additionally, the researchers introduced Category-Equivariant Neural Networks (CENN), which further generalize equivariant neural networks to leverage categorical symmetries, including non-invertible symmetries with compositional relations. This work advances the theoretical foundations of equivariant deep learning and opens pathways for exploiting complex symmetry structures in data.

item.title: Researchers propose SAGE framework to automate discovery of latent vulnerabilities in LLM-based Text-to-SQL models, revealing widespread fragility and cross-model weaknesses [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced SAGE (Systematic Automated Guided Exploration), a new framework designed to automatically identify hidden vulnerabilities in Large Language Model (LLM)-based Text-to-SQL systems. By generating hypotheses about potential weaknesses and using a dynamic Vulnerability Codex to create targeted tests, SAGE systematically uncovers failure patterns that reveal significant fragility in current models. This approach moves beyond traditional static, expert-defined diagnostic methods, enabling more thorough and automated exploration of model reliability. Extensive testing on leading open-source LLMs demonstrated that SAGE detects numerous failure cases, with the Vulnerability Codex showing strong applicability across different models, indicating common structural weaknesses. Preliminary experiments also suggest that lightweight fine-tuning using the identified vulnerabilities can improve model robustness, pointing toward a scalable method for enhancing the reliability of Text-to-SQL systems in future applications.

item.title: Researchers evaluate medieval Latin manuscript translation pipelines, finding specialized OCR models feeding directly into vision-language models outperform complex multi-component systems on a new 1,383-line dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a systematic framework to evaluate translation pipelines for medieval Latin manuscripts, revealing that specialized Optical Character Recognition (OCR) models combined directly with vision-language models (VLMs) outperform more complex multi-component systems. Their study, conducted on the new Interpres-Parallel-Corpus (IPC) dataset of 1,383 aligned manuscript lines with transcriptions and expert translations, highlights challenges such as scribal shorthand, ligatures, and parchment degradation that complicate machine translation in this historical context. Benchmarking on the CATMuS Latin dataset showed that domain-specific OCR models significantly reduce character error rates compared to general-purpose VLMs, despite having fewer parameters. The researchers found that adding techniques like retrieval-augmented generation or post-OCR correction can introduce errors and reduce overall translation quality, suggesting that simpler pipelines may be more effective for low-resource historical manuscript translation tasks. These findings provide a valuable benchmark and practical guidance for deploying translation systems in challenging historical settings, emphasizing the importance of specialized OCR models and streamlined processing to improve accuracy and efficiency in translating medieval Latin texts.

item.title: Researchers evaluate nine LLMs on communicating probabilistic risk in natural language, finding consistent but miscalibrated outputs with weaker uncertainty performance, limiting zero-shot risk communication reliability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated nine large language models (LLMs) to determine their ability to communicate probabilistic risk in natural language. The study tested whether these models could consistently produce accurate verbal descriptions that reflect the magnitude of underlying numerical probabilities and uncertainties. Results showed that while LLMs were generally consistent in their outputs, they were miscalibrated and performed significantly worse in conveying uncertainty compared to likelihood, limiting their reliability for zero-shot risk communication. The evaluation involved simulating probabilistic outputs from an upstream model using a Beta distribution and prompting LLMs across various domain contexts and temperature settings. Providing LLMs with summary statistics reduced sensitivity to context but did not fix the miscalibration, indicating that the main challenge lies in the verbalization process itself. These findings suggest that current LLMs are not yet dependable standalone tools for communicating probabilistic predictions in natural language.

item.title: Researchers propose MPSelectTune, a prompt-type selection method for fine-tuning that improves concept unlearning and main task accuracy in large language models across four benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MPSelectTune, a novel fine-tuning method for large language models (LLMs) that enhances the removal of biased or harmful concepts while improving main task accuracy. This approach addresses the challenge of concept unlearning across different prompt types by focusing on the "worst prompt type"-the prompt with the highest concept accuracy-to guide fine-tuning. MPSelectTune employs a two-stage process that minimizes concept accuracy for this prompt type using a multi-task loss function. Experimental results on four benchmarks demonstrate that MPSelectTune achieves a 2 to 15% improvement in main task accuracy compared to recent baselines, while reducing the worst-case concept accuracy by up to 17%. This method offers a more robust way to mitigate unsafe or unethical responses in LLMs caused by undesirable pre-trained concepts, advancing the reliability and safety of prompt-based model adaptation.

item.title: Study validates Natural Language Tools framework across 14 AI models, showing 14.9pp accuracy improvement and 93% error reduction compared to structured tool calling [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A recent study independently replicates and extends the Natural Language Tools (NLT) framework, evaluating its performance across 14 large language models in 8,560 trials. The research confirms that NLT improves tool-calling accuracy by 14.9 percentage points compared to structured tool calling and reduces critical errors by 93%. These benefits vary with model capability, with smaller and reasoning models gaining the most, while highly optimized frontier models show smaller or reversed advantages. The study also finds that NLT decreases token usage by 25.2% and enhances reliability and efficiency in recursive agentic workflows by avoiding the overhead caused by structured tool-calling failures. This work provides the first independent validation of NLT using open-source tools, highlights how model capability influences its effectiveness, and emphasizes its significant reliability improvements, making NLT a practical alternative for production systems prioritizing reliability over parseability.

item.title: Researchers introduce NormWorlds-CF, a solver-verified environment for counterfactual normative reasoning with metamorphic-relation GRPO, improving accuracy and evaluation without LLM judges in 270 root families and 1080 paired tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed NormWorlds-CF, a solver-verified environment designed for counterfactual normative reasoning within executable rule-based worlds. This system uses a deterministic solver to generate final answers along with proof and falsification certificates, argument statuses, support sets, and paired-world change labels, enabling evaluation without relying on large language model judges. The benchmark includes a comprehensive set of tasks involving 270 root families and 1080 paired canonical-to-variant cases, facilitating detailed supervision and assessment. The study reveals that training solely on final answers is insufficient, as models can achieve perfect accuracy on answer tasks but fail on falsification tasks. Incorporating proof and falsification training with targeted replay improves overall accuracy. Additionally, the researchers introduce metamorphic-relation GRPO (MR-GRPO), a class-conditioned reward mechanism that provides partial credit for relation families and solver-visible changes. Experiments demonstrate that MR-GRPO enhances relation accuracy and reduces errors compared to other reward strategies, delivering balanced performance across multiple evaluation metrics. These findings highlight the importance of verified counterfactual structures in guiding post-training processes beyond final answers. However, challenges remain in generating exact full change records, recognizing invariant subtypes, and achieving robust out-of-distribution transfer, indicating areas for future research.

item.title: Researchers propose Order-based Causal Discovery for Multistage Processes (OCDM) using structural knowledge and neural network pruning to improve causal inference and efficiency on large multistage datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new method called Order-based Causal Discovery for Multistage Processes (OCDM) to improve causal inference in complex, multistage datasets. OCDM integrates structural knowledge about the stages of a process to better infer causal relationships while maintaining the hierarchical and sequential nature of the data. The approach also includes a novel pruning technique using stochastic gated neural networks to enhance computational efficiency and reduce spurious connections in the causal graph. OCDM addresses limitations of existing causal discovery methods that can yield counterintuitive results or struggle with large datasets typical of multistage processes. Experiments on various datasets demonstrate that OCDM outperforms current methods in accurately uncovering the causal structure of multistage systems, offering a more reliable and efficient tool for analyzing complex processes.

item.title: Researchers release BanglaMemeEvidence, a multimodal dataset of 2,917 Bengali memes with annotations for explanatory evidence detection, and propose BengaliMemeEvidenceNet achieving 0.74 F1 score [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced BanglaMemeEvidence, a new multimodal dataset comprising 2,917 Bengali memes annotated with natural language explanations to support the task of explanatory evidence detection. This dataset includes detailed annotations such as Meme OCR, Meme Context, and Evidence Sentences, along with relevance scores that link the memes to their explanations. To analyze these memes effectively, the team proposed BengaliMemeEvidenceNet, a hybrid multimodal framework that combines textual and visual features, achieving an F1 score of 0.74 in their experiments. This work addresses challenges in understanding memes, particularly in low-resource languages like Bengali, by focusing on identifying sentences that clarify a meme's meaning and humor. The dataset and model represent a significant advancement in meme analysis, especially for tasks involving harmful content detection, cyberbullying identification, and sentiment analysis, which require deeper contextual understanding. This study marks the first effort to tackle evidence detection in Bengali memes, providing a valuable resource for future research in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose CrossBERT architecture separating representation learning from token reconstruction to improve text encoder scalability and efficiency, showing superior performance on MTEB and GLUE benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CrossBERT, a novel text encoder architecture that separates representation learning from token reconstruction to address limitations in traditional BERT encoders. This two-part design allows for higher masking ratios and improved gradient collection, resulting in increased throughput and sample efficiency. CrossBERT demonstrates consistent scaling and outperforms existing models on benchmarks such as MTEB and frozen GLUE. The study highlights that BERT's flat architecture, which ties representation learning directly to token reconstruction loss, leads to representations that become less exploitable by frozen probes despite better perplexity scores. By decoupling these processes, CrossBERT enables more effective training strategies, including a Complementary Masking Strategy that enhances performance and efficiency. This advancement suggests a promising direction for scalable and efficient text encoding, potentially impacting future natural language processing models by improving both their training dynamics and downstream task performance.

item.title: Researchers compare tabular foundation models and conventional machine learning for crowd-state classification at Hajj and Umrah, highlighting accuracy and efficiency trade-offs based on label availability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated tabular foundation models against conventional machine learning methods for classifying crowd states during Hajj and Umrah, focusing on scenarios with limited labeled data. Their study found that foundation models perform better when very few labels are available, while tuned conventional models surpass them as more labeled data becomes accessible. The comparison also highlighted efficiency differences, with foundation models avoiding the high tuning costs of conventional methods but requiring context reprocessing for each prediction. The analysis used three real datasets and tested various models in both tuned and untuned forms. Results indicate that no single approach is universally superior; the optimal choice depends on the available label and computational budgets. This work provides practical guidance for selecting machine learning strategies in contexts where labeling is costly and data is scarce.

item.title: Researchers propose a unified algebraic framework for classification performance evaluation covering binary, multiclass, multilabel, ordinal, hierarchical, cost-sensitive, and soft-label settings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a unified algebraic framework for evaluating classification performance that integrates various settings including binary, multiclass, multilabel, ordinal, hierarchical, cost-sensitive, and soft-label classifications. This framework represents actual and predicted labels as binary indicator matrices and uses three aggregation operators corresponding to micro, macro/weighted, and exemplar averaging. It extends any binary performance measure to all classification types without requiring measure-specific derivations and supports soft classifier outputs, soft ground truth, ordinal classification, and cost-sensitive evaluation. The framework establishes several theoretical results, such as the equivalence of micro-averaging and denominator-weighted macro-averaging, the uniqueness of the product t-norm in preserving confusion-matrix partitions, and characterizations of skew-invariant measures. It also shows that micro-precision, micro-recall, and micro-F1 are equal to accuracy in multiclass settings. Empirical tests on synthetic and real datasets confirm these theoretical findings, demonstrating the framework's broad applicability and robustness in classification performance evaluation.

item.title: Researchers introduce ParCFDFinder in Desbordante to speed up conditional functional dependency discovery by up to 318× and reduce memory usage on large datasets
item.description: Researchers have developed ParCFDFinder, an enhanced algorithm integrated into the open-source data profiler Desbordante, to improve the discovery of conditional functional dependencies (CFDs). CFDs are important for data quality and integrity by specifying context-dependent data constraints. ParCFDFinder introduces algorithmic and engineering improvements, including parallelization, resulting in speed increases of up to 318 times and memory reductions up to 23 times compared to previous implementations. Desbordante, written in C++ with a Python interface, allows users to efficiently discover CFDs on large datasets with hundreds of thousands of rows using standard hardware. This advancement makes it feasible to perform complex data profiling tasks more quickly and with less resource consumption, facilitating better data management and analysis in practical settings.

item.title: Researchers present OmniOpt, a unified taxonomy and benchmark for over 100 modern optimizers across model scales and training regimes, detailing mechanisms and training objectives [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced OmniOpt, a comprehensive taxonomy and benchmark that unifies over 100 modern optimization methods used in large-scale model training. OmniOpt organizes optimizers through a five-stage meta-pipeline and employs norm-constrained linear minimization oracles to classify methods by their mechanisms and training objectives. This framework provides a systematic analysis across various model scales and training regimes, including language model pretraining and image classification. The study presents a dual-dimension taxonomy that categorizes optimizers by their underlying mechanisms and the measurable objectives they target. By benchmarking representative optimizers across diverse tasks, OmniOpt highlights the trade-offs and performance characteristics of different method families. This work offers the research community a structured approach to selecting optimizers based on explicit assumptions and guides future developments in optimization techniques for machine learning.

item.title: Researchers introduce Reward-Gated On-Policy Distillation (RG-OPD) to improve student model training by filtering unreliable teacher signals using verifier feedback, outperforming existing distillation methods on reasoning and coding benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Reward-Gated On-Policy Distillation (RG-OPD), a method that enhances the training of smaller student models by selectively trusting teacher model signals based on verifier feedback. This approach addresses the issue of unreliable teacher supervision, which can sometimes reinforce incorrect solutions or suppress valid student reasoning paths. RG-OPD combines sparse verifier rewards with dense teacher guidance to filter misleading information while maintaining detailed token-level supervision. Testing RG-OPD on reasoning and coding benchmarks demonstrated its superiority over existing distillation techniques, including vanilla reverse-KL distillation and the TSD-KD baseline. The method showed notable improvements in performance metrics, particularly in long-generation tasks, indicating its potential to produce more accurate and robust student models. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration and application.

item.title: Researchers propose speaker-disentangled chunk-wise regression method for unsupervised syllabic tokenization, achieving state-of-the-art syllable boundary detection and improved language model performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new speaker-disentangled chunk-wise regression method for unsupervised syllabic tokenization, which improves the identification of syllable boundaries and the clustering of syllabic segments from raw speech. This approach addresses the issue of models capturing speaker identity instead of linguistic content by regressing speaker-perturbed student representations toward clean teacher targets within fixed-length chunks. The method achieves state-of-the-art results in syllable boundary detection and enhances language model performance, with a speech language model trained on these tokens showing a 7% relative improvement in syntactic and semantic understanding compared to previous phone-level models.

item.title: Researchers propose an online geometry-aware token pruning method for 3D question answering that reduces token usage by up to 50% and improves performance on ScanQA, SQA3D, and OpenEQA-HM3D benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an online geometry-aware token pruning method to enhance 3D question answering with Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs). This approach reduces token usage by up to 50% by projecting input frames into a shared voxel space and pruning redundant image tokens before processing, enabling more efficient inference without additional training or high memory demands. The method improves performance on benchmarks including ScanQA, SQA3D, and OpenEQA-HM3D when applied to models like Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B. Unlike previous offline techniques that require preprocessing all scene frames, this online method integrates seamlessly with existing MLLMs and leverages depth and camera pose information to identify overlapping spatial regions across multiple views. This innovation addresses the computational challenges of extending 2D question answering models to 3D environments, facilitating faster and more resource-efficient processing.

item.title: Researchers propose FedSPM, a routing-enabled semiparametric mixture framework for federated learning addressing dual heterogeneity in client data, demonstrating improved routing and prediction on medical benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced FedSPM, a novel federated learning framework designed to address dual heterogeneity in client data by incorporating routing-enabled semiparametric mixture modeling. This approach recognizes both inter-client and intra-client variability, such as distinct disease subtypes within the same hospital, and improves the routing of queries to the most appropriate client for prediction. FedSPM combines predictive and feature distributions for each client-specific latent component and uses a federated expectation-maximization algorithm to optimize performance, demonstrating enhanced routing and prediction accuracy on medical datasets and controlled benchmarks. The framework models feature distributions through density ratios relative to a common nonparametric measure estimated via empirical likelihood, allowing flexible modeling while sharing information across clients. The researchers also provide theoretical convergence guarantees for their algorithm. Experimental results confirm that FedSPM effectively manages the complexities of dual heterogeneity, leading to consistent improvements over existing methods in federated learning scenarios involving heterogeneous medical data.

item.title: Researchers propose Parametric Memory Decoding framework and PMDRouter for zero-shot routing in LoRA-based External Parametric Memory, demonstrating improved performance on PMD-Bench [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Parametric Memory Decoding (PMD), a new framework designed to improve zero-shot routing in LoRA-based External Parametric Memory (EPM) systems without the need for additional routing components. They also developed PMDRouter, a method that evaluates each LoRA module based on its response magnitude from a single base-model prefill. Experiments on the newly organized PMD-Bench, which includes document-level, domain-level, and task-skill evaluations, demonstrate that PMDRouter outperforms existing zero-shot routing methods across multiple settings. The study addresses challenges in current zero-shot LoRA routing methods, such as scattered evaluations and the lack of a unified routing signal perspective. By reframing routing as decoding activations over external parametric memory, PMD provides a systematic approach to enhance routing performance. The results suggest that zero-shot routing in LoRA-based EPM is feasible and that PMD could serve as a general framework for future improvements in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose mask-based self-supervised task with transformers to improve sample efficiency in vision-based deep reinforcement learning, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on control benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a mask-based self-supervised learning task combined with transformers to enhance sample efficiency in vision-based deep reinforcement learning. This approach uses mask prediction as an auxiliary task, enabling the model to leverage sequence and context information to predict masked inputs, thereby improving the agent's understanding and representation learning. The method reconstructs masked input sequences in latent space and, when integrated with reinforcement learning models, leads to better sample efficiency and outperforms current state-of-the-art methods on various continuous and discrete control benchmarks. The proposed technique addresses the challenge of extracting effective states from high-dimensional image inputs with limited samples, a common issue in vision-based reinforcement learning. By focusing on non-reconstruction mask prediction rather than traditional reconstruction tasks, the model strengthens task comprehension and representation quality. This advancement demonstrates significant improvements in learning efficiency across multiple control tasks, suggesting a promising direction for future reinforcement learning research.

item.title: Researchers propose hierarchical multi-to-single-modal knowledge distillation for efficient plasma disruption prediction on EAST dataset, preserving multimodal advantages while reducing inference cost [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a hierarchical multi-to-single-modal knowledge distillation framework to improve plasma disruption prediction in tokamak reactors using the EAST dataset. This approach trains a multimodal teacher model with both time-series diagnostic signals and visible images to capture disruption precursors, then transfers this knowledge to a time-series-only student model for inference, significantly reducing computational costs while maintaining predictive accuracy. The framework employs Transformer-based encoders and a prototype-guided spatiotemporal hypergraph module during training, with knowledge distilled at graph-structure, representation, and decision levels. Tested on 640 discharges from the EAST dataset, the method preserves the advantages of multimodal learning and offers an efficient solution for disruption prediction. The researchers plan to release the source code publicly to support further development in this area.

item.title: Researchers introduce SensorGen, a large-scale study evaluating generative models for real-world sensor time series across 14 settings, 7 datasets, and 12 signal modalities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced SensorGen, a comprehensive study evaluating generative models for real-world sensor time series data across 14 settings, 7 datasets, and 12 signal modalities. This study addresses the fragmented state of generative modeling for sensor data by systematically assessing models from five major families to understand their performance and limitations in practical scenarios. SensorGen reveals that flow-matching models generally perform well across diverse settings, while specific signal properties influence model effectiveness, such as demographic covariates enhancing longitudinal data generation and time-frequency modeling benefiting high-frequency signals. The study also highlights that generated sensor signals have practical applications beyond visual realism, with improvements in generation quality and downstream task performance through scaling and synthetic data use. By establishing a broader understanding of design choices, evaluation protocols, and failure modes, SensorGen provides valuable insights for advancing generative modeling techniques in continuous, high-dimensional, and noisy sensor time series data, which are common in many real-world systems.

item.title: Researchers present FreshCache, a risk-constrained semantic caching system for open-web retrieval-augmented LLMs that models data freshness and reduces stale errors while saving up to 98% of search API calls [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed FreshCache, a semantic caching system designed for open-web retrieval-augmented large language models (LLMs) that accounts for data freshness to reduce stale errors while significantly cutting search API calls. FreshCache uses a three-tier approach that estimates the probability of cached results being outdated through a temporal inference model enhanced by a learned multilayer perceptron (MLP), allowing it to approve cache reuse only when the risk of staleness is within predefined error budgets. This method enables a gradual degradation of cache validity over time instead of a strict binary decision between stale cache hits and full retrieval. The team introduced FreshCache-Bench, a benchmark dataset with over 8,000 queries across multiple freshness categories, validated against real web snapshots taken at intervals up to seven days. At a 24-hour evaluation, FreshCache with the MLP model achieved 97% savings in search API calls with a minimal stale error rate of 0.1%, outperforming existing methods such as SemanticTTL, vCache, and SCALM. Further analysis showed that only a small fraction of detected content changes actually impacted answer correctness, indicating a very low true stale error rate. The system's temporal risk gating and learned model contributed to significant reductions in stale errors compared to similarity-only caching approaches.

item.title: Researchers develop fixed-confidence best-arm identification algorithm for causal mediation analysis with sample-efficient, high-probability correctness guarantees, validated on large-scale advertising data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a fixed-confidence best-arm identification algorithm designed to maximize the expected natural direct potential outcome (NDPO) in causal mediation analysis. This approach isolates the effect of an intervention by excluding pathways through mediators that may be irrelevant or confounding. The algorithm, based on the Track-and-Stop framework and employing a cutting-set method, ensures sample-efficient identification with high-probability correctness guarantees, achieving both \(\delta\)-correctness and asymptotic optimality. The team first established population-level identification of the expected NDPO within a causal bandit setting using observable interventional distributions. They then validated their method through empirical evaluations on a large-scale real-world advertising dataset (IPinYou), demonstrating its practical effectiveness in complex data environments.

item.title: Researchers present a unified membership inference framework for generative models across text-to-text, text-to-image, and image-to-text modalities with superior black-box attack performance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a unified membership inference framework that applies across multiple generative model modalities, including text-to-text, text-to-image, and image-to-text. This framework addresses privacy risks by determining whether specific data points were used in a model's training set, improving upon previous methods that were limited to individual model types. The approach leverages the observation that a generative model's output distribution can approximate its training data distribution, enabling membership inference through likelihood ratio testing in a shared embedding space. The team conducted extensive experiments under strict black-box conditions, considering both partial-knowledge and zero-knowledge threat models, and evaluated the method against data used for fine-tuning and pre-training. Results show that this unified framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, which are typically optimized for single model classes, demonstrating its broad applicability and enhanced effectiveness in protecting privacy across diverse generative models.

item.title: Researchers propose Full-Stack FP4, a stable NVFP4 framework for 4-bit LLM pretraining addressing quantization noise in projections, optimizers, and attention with near-BF16 performance on 3B/64B-token models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Full-Stack FP4, a comprehensive framework for stable 4-bit large language model (LLM) pretraining that addresses quantization noise issues in transformer linear layers, optimizer states, and attention mechanisms. This approach employs module-specific precision strategies, including LoRA-SVD decomposition for linear projections, a robust AdamW second-moment transformation for optimizers, and a mixed-precision scheme for attention, achieving near-BF16 performance with only a 1.47% loss gap on 3 billion parameter models trained over 64 billion tokens. The framework tackles unique numerical challenges such as error amplification in linear layers, fragility of optimizer second moments to low-precision denominators, and the need for strict forward-backward quantization consistency in attention computations. By integrating these solutions into a plug-and-play system, Full-Stack FP4 enables efficient and stable end-to-end NVFP4 pretraining, demonstrating significant improvements in stability and efficiency compared to previous methods.

item.title: Researchers introduce dOPSD, an on-policy self-distillation method for diffusion language models that improves math reasoning and code generation by deriving teacher privilege from the model's own decoding trajectory [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed dOPSD, an on-policy self-distillation method for diffusion large language models (dLLMs) that enhances their reasoning abilities in math and code generation tasks. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on external ground-truth references, dOPSD derives the teacher model's privileged information from the student's own decoding trajectory, allowing the model to improve by evaluating its own intermediate outputs. This method outperforms existing supervised and on-policy baselines on benchmarks such as Dream and LLaDA.

item.title: Researchers release evalci, a Python library for statistically rigorous comparison of language model evaluations with confidence intervals and significance tests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced evalci, a Python library designed to provide statistically rigorous comparisons of language model evaluations by incorporating confidence intervals and significance tests. This tool addresses the common issue in language model benchmarking where differences in accuracy are reported without assessing whether these gaps could be due to sampling noise, potentially overstating the confidence in model comparisons. Evalci processes per-item results tables to generate publication-ready statistical claims, supporting adapters for popular evaluation frameworks and validating its routines against independent references. The library includes features such as paired permutation tests, multiple-comparison corrections, and power analysis, all implemented using standard Python packages like numpy, scipy, and pandas. A case study using evalci re-examined the MMLU benchmark results of nine language models, revealing that several adjacent rank differences on the leaderboard were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Evalci is available for installation via PyPI and its source code is accessible on GitHub.

item.title: Researchers establish statistical guarantees and applications for pairwise quantile regression with theoretical bounds and facial recognition error analysis [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a statistical framework for pairwise quantile regression, extending traditional quantile regression to analyze similarity functions between pairs of independent observations, such as biometric data from pixelated ID photos. They provide theoretical guarantees for this approach by treating it as an empirical minimization problem using a pairwise pinball loss, and establish generalization bounds with conditions for fast learning rates. The methodology is supported by simulation experiments and is applied to analyze errors in facial recognition similarity scoring. The study leverages advanced concentration results for U-processes to underpin the statistical learning problem and confirms the practical validity of the approach through empirical evidence. This work offers a novel tool for understanding conditional distributions in contexts where the response variable is a similarity measure, broadening the applicability of quantile regression techniques. By applying this framework to facial recognition error analysis, the researchers demonstrate its potential to improve biometric system assessments, providing insights into error patterns and contributing to more reliable similarity scoring methods in biometric applications.

item.title: Researchers show covert trait propagation enables student models trained on noise to inherit teacher representations through geometric alignment in MLP distillation on MNIST [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that a student neural network model trained solely on uniform noise can still acquire its teacher model's digit-classification capabilities if both models share the same initialization. This phenomenon, studied in a multilayer perceptron (MLP) distillation setting on the MNIST dataset, is driven by a process called covert trait propagation (CTP), where geometric alignment between the student and teacher models enables the transfer of learned representations. Key experiments reveal that alignment of specific network projections is crucial for this transfer, and that the mechanism is not purely informational but depends on geometric factors within the network. The study further explores how shared initialization creates a common coordinate system that facilitates alignment through gradient updates, and validates the mechanism through multiple experiments including the effects of freezing certain network components and analyzing multi-teacher ensembles. Extending this geometric perspective to instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs), the researchers identify similar alignment effects activated by training, while also noting that some commonly used metrics may introduce artifacts in interpreting these behaviors.

item.title: Wan-Streamer v0.2 raises interactive output resolution to 640x368 while preserving 200 ms model latency and 550 ms total remote interaction latency with multi-GPU architecture [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Wan-Streamer v0.2 is an upgraded audio-visual interaction model that increases the interactive output resolution from 192x336 to 640x368 while maintaining a model-side latency of about 200 milliseconds at 25 frames per second. This enhancement allows for clearer visualization of agents' posture, gaze, hands, and surrounding scene elements during real-time conversations without increasing user-visible delay. The system achieves this by retaining a single-GPU low-latency path for perception and language processing, while employing a multi-GPU architecture for the more demanding visual generation tasks. This design splits the high-resolution video sequence across multiple GPUs for efficient processing, preserving a compact interface between components and keeping total remote interaction latency around 550 milliseconds, including network communication time.

item.title: Researchers develop deep learning surrogate model to accelerate ASTEC nuclear reactor severe accident simulations, predicting 80 variables up to 40 hours in under a minute [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a deep learning surrogate model to significantly accelerate simulations of severe accidents in nuclear reactors using the ASTEC code. This model combines an AutoEncoder for dimensionality reduction and a Neural Ordinary Differential Equation for time-stepping, enabling the prediction of around 80 physical variables simultaneously. The surrogate model can simulate up to 40 hours of reactor accident scenarios in under a minute, compared to several days required by traditional methods, making it suitable for real-time applications such as operator training. The surrogate model was trained on data generated by the ASTEC simulator for scenarios including station blackout and loss-of-coolant accidents. It maintains stable predictions over long time horizons and achieves a dimensionality reduction factor of over 300, allowing efficient computation on both CPUs and GPUs.
