This study represents the first exploration of deep learning surrogate modeling to approximate the complex, nonlinear physics involved in severe nuclear reactor accidents as modeled by ASTEC.

item.title: Researchers introduce operator-on-F as a complementary diagnostic to value-equivalence for evaluating latent world models in model-based reinforcement learning, showing strong correlation with planning return loss [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced operator-on-F, a new diagnostic tool designed to complement traditional value-equivalence methods for evaluating latent world models in model-based reinforcement learning. This approach compares a model's k-step latent pushforward to the environment's on an observable subset, providing a more sensitive measure of planning-relevant errors that are often missed by reward and value prediction metrics. The study demonstrates that operator-on-F correlates strongly with planning return loss, outperforming conventional error measures in distinguishing model performance across different sizes and architectures. In experiments involving a TD-MPC2 size sweep on the cheetah-run task, reward-prediction errors showed limited variation and weak correlation with return, while operator error varied widely and closely tracked declines in planning return. At larger model sizes, operator error increased significantly, coinciding with a collapse in planning return, despite reward-prediction error remaining within a narrow range. The operator diagnostic also effectively differentiated between architectures, highlighting its utility as a complementary evaluation tool rather than a replacement for existing methods.

item.title: Researchers propose stabilisation strategies for LLM-augmented cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning to address regime-dependent failures caused by dynamic reward weight updates [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified challenges in integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), specifically when dynamically updating LLM-generated reward weights during training. This practice violates the stationarity assumption of Potential-Based Reward Shaping (PBRS) and contaminates the experience replay buffer, leading to regime-dependent failures that vary based on the baseline system's competence. To address this, the team proposed two stabilization methods: a Phase-Based Freeze Schedule to maintain stationarity during training phases and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) smoothing to limit reward weight fluctuations. The researchers tested these strategies across three cooperative environments using QMIX and an exploratory VDN extension, identifying three distinct regimes. In the augmentative regime, where the baseline performs moderately well, EMA improved success rates significantly, while naive dynamic updates caused performance collapse. In the essential regime, where the baseline fails, any shaping enabled task completion. In the supplementary regime, where the baseline is nearly optimal, stabilized shaping maintained performance without adding variance. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining reward-signal stationarity and suggest that understanding the regime can predict whether dynamic LLM shaping will be beneficial or detrimental.

item.title: Researchers propose PulmoSight-XAI, an explainable multi-view attention ensemble with gradient boosting meta-learning achieving state-of-the-art multi-label chest X-ray classification on 14 thoracic pathologies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PulmoSight-XAI, an explainable multi-view ensemble framework that combines attention mechanisms and gradient boosting meta-learning to classify 14 thoracic pathologies from chest X-rays. The system independently analyzes frontal and lateral radiographs using multiple convolutional neural networks enhanced with multi-scale feature fusion and attention modules, addressing challenges like class imbalance and co-occurring diseases. Evaluated on a large dataset, it achieved state-of-the-art performance with high AUROC scores and demonstrated strong anatomical consistency through various explainability techniques. The framework employs a novel hybrid loss function to handle class imbalance and integrates test-time augmentation predictions and uncertainty measures into hierarchical meta-learners, including XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, followed by optimized stacking. This approach preserves fine-grained features and emphasizes pathology-specific information, providing a transparent and clinically practical tool for automated thoracic disease diagnosis.

item.title: Researchers analyze encoder probing and decoder attribution methods for neural multi-attribute vehicle routing problem solvers using Hard-Mask and Recourse decoders, revealing differences in constraint representation and policy feasibility [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have examined neural autoregressive solvers for the Multi-Attribute Vehicle Routing Problem (MAVRP), focusing on understanding how these models represent constraints and justify decisions at each step. They analyzed encoder representations using various probing techniques and evaluated decoder attribution methods through gradient-based approaches, assessing explanations for fidelity, stability, and actionability. Their study compared six model variants combining different encoders and decoders, revealing that graph inductive biases enhance representation and explanation quality, and that certain training regimes enable models to better handle infeasibility by producing useful counterfactuals. The research highlights differences between encoder types, such as the Mixture-of-Experts encoder's distributed constraint representation, and contrasts two decoder approaches-Hard-Mask and Recourse-showing that Recourse-trained policies more effectively represent infeasibility and generate feasible alternatives. These insights provide a deeper understanding of how neural solvers process complex routing constraints and offer interpretable justifications, which is valuable for dispatchers who need to validate or compare routing decisions.

item.title: Researchers find GPT-4 can learn the principled-versus-statistical distinction from language, while earlier models struggle despite sensitivity to statistical prevalence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have investigated whether language models can learn to distinguish between principled truths, which hold by category membership, and statistical truths, which hold due to frequency. While earlier models showed sensitivity to statistical prevalence, they struggled to represent this core conceptual distinction. The study found that GPT-4 is the first model to successfully learn the principled-versus-statistical distinction from language alone. This finding suggests that advanced language models like GPT-4 may be capable of acquiring sophisticated causal and conceptual knowledge directly from linguistic input, potentially bootstrapping fundamental human-like conceptual distinctions through language experience. The research highlights a significant step forward in understanding how AI models process and internalize complex semantic concepts beyond mere statistical patterns.

item.title: Researchers formalize concept representations and contextual transformations as shared geometric structures in large language models across six model families [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a framework to understand how large language models represent and transform concepts using shared geometric structures. By modeling concepts as point-cloud manifolds and contextual transformations as vector fields, they analyzed six different language model families and found that context affects each concept uniquely. This variation in concept displacement is semantically organized and consistent across models, indicating a common underlying geometry in how concepts and their contextual changes are represented. The study reveals that not only are concept representations shared among models, but the way context transforms these concepts follows a structured pattern linked to semantic properties like lexical concreteness and density. This shared geometric structure allows displacement patterns from one model to predict those in others, suggesting a richer and more organized representation of concepts and context in language models than previously recognized.

item.title: Researchers propose Lyapunov-stabilised quantisation framework for fixed-point neural networks to prevent activation overflow and improve accuracy on MNIST with 4-16 bit precision [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a Lyapunov-stabilised quantisation framework to improve the reliability of low-precision neural networks using fixed-point arithmetic, which often suffers from activation overflow and accuracy loss due to two's-complement overflow wrapping. This approach monitors hidden-state energy with a layerwise Lyapunov function and applies a monotone projection to maintain bounded and stable state evolution, effectively preventing activation overflow during training and inference. The method was tested on the MNIST dataset using a compact patch-based transformer with bit-widths ranging from 4 to 16 bits. Results showed that traditional quantisation-aware training without constraints led to high activation overflow rates and near-chance accuracy, while the proposed Lyapunov projection reduced overflow to below 0.012% and restored stable learning, achieving 86.55% accuracy at 12 bits. This demonstrates that Lyapunov-based control can serve as a hardware-aware stabilization mechanism for fixed-point neural networks, enhancing their performance on resource-constrained devices.

item.title: Researchers present CRISP, a spatiotemporal camera-radar backbone pretrained via forecasting-based world-model learning for autonomous driving, improving long-horizon point cloud forecasting and downstream tasks on nuScenes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CRISP, a spatiotemporal camera-radar backbone designed for autonomous driving that is pretrained using forecasting-based world-model learning. CRISP generates a unified bird's-eye-view representation by predicting future LiDAR point clouds from historical multi-view images and radar data, using LiDAR only during pretraining. This approach enhances long-horizon point cloud forecasting and improves performance on various downstream tasks such as 3D detection, tracking, mapping, motion forecasting, and planning, using only camera and radar inputs during deployment. To optimize forecasting-based pretraining for camera-radar fusion, CRISP incorporates an enhanced radar encoder, radar-enhanced temporal self-attention, and multimodal feature rendering with modality innovation gating. These innovations enable the model to effectively integrate radar range and Doppler information with camera data, improving temporal propagation in the bird's-eye-view representation. Experiments on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate CRISP's effectiveness and suggest that predictive camera-radar pretraining offers a scalable solution for autonomous driving under practical sensor configurations.

item.title: Researchers present Auto, an AGI compiler that records and compiles LLM agent behavior into verified WebAssembly binaries, achieving 6.4x cost reduction and 96.9% parity on AUTO-BENCH benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Auto, an AGI compiler that records the behavior of large language model (LLM) agents and compiles deterministic parts into verified WebAssembly binaries. This approach reduces computational costs by 6.4 times while maintaining 96.9% accuracy on the AUTO-BENCH benchmark, which measures agent performance across various tasks. Auto uses a tiered runtime with calibrated guards to ensure correctness and recompiles behavior traces to avoid redundant computation. Auto identifies deterministic segments of agent behavior and converts them into permanent, verified programs that run efficiently in a sandboxed environment. Testing on a 300-item task stream with distribution shifts demonstrated significant cost savings and near-parity performance compared to the original agent. The system also highlights challenges related to guard calibration and reference fidelity, which affect the reliability of compiled outputs. The project code is available on GitHub for further exploration.

item.title: Researchers present Mask2Real-WM, a two-stage action-conditioned world model using segmentation masks to improve sim-to-real transfer for dexterous robotic manipulation with 23 degrees of freedom [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Mask2Real-WM, a two-stage action-conditioned world model designed to improve sim-to-real transfer in dexterous robotic manipulation involving 23 degrees of freedom. The model separates pixel prediction into a dynamics model that forecasts future segmentation masks based on past masks and action sequences, and a rendering model that converts these masks into photorealistic RGB images using an advanced diffusion backbone. This approach reduces the simulation-to-reality gap by leveraging segmentation masks, allowing extensive pretraining on synthetic data followed by fine-tuning with limited real-world demonstrations. Experiments on a dexterous pick-and-place task demonstrate that both mask conditioning and simulation pretraining are essential for precise control over each degree of freedom. Unlike monolithic models that capture general hand and end-effector movements, Mask2Real-WM reliably reflects fine-grained, per-joint action effects, highlighting its potential for enhancing robotic manipulation accuracy and control.

item.title: Researchers propose PREDIKTOR, a multi-view framework aligning patient-specific gene regulatory networks and transcriptomic perturbation profiles to predict clinical drug response, outperforming baselines on TCGA and I-SPY2 trial data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PREDIKTOR, a multi-view framework designed to predict patient-specific clinical drug responses by aligning personalized gene regulatory networks with simulated transcriptomic perturbation profiles. This approach integrates individualized gene networks derived from tumor expression data with drug-target information and uses a graph neural encoder alongside a pretrained gene-gene attention model to generate mechanistically informed embeddings. PREDIKTOR demonstrated superior performance compared to existing methods on TCGA datasets and showed effective zero-shot transfer to the I-SPY2 clinical trial data, improving prediction accuracy by 5.6% in AUROC. The framework constructs patient-specific gene regulatory networks using DysRegNet and incorporates drug-target links from DrugBank to create a drug-centric embedding. Simultaneously, it simulates post-treatment transcriptomic profiles using a model pretrained on LINCS L1000 data. These two views are aligned in a shared latent space through a contrastive learning objective, enabling end-to-end classification of therapeutic response. The aligned embeddings also provide stable gene and pathway attributions that correspond to known biological mechanisms, enhancing interpretability and supporting precision oncology applications.

item.title: Researchers propose cost-efficient on-policy data augmentation using few teacher steps at learner-induced contexts to improve LLM agent post-training across HotpotQA, ALFWorld, and Terminal-Bench-Dev [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a cost-efficient method for on-policy data augmentation to improve the post-training of large language model (LLM) agents. Their approach focuses on using a few teacher-generated steps at learner-induced contexts rather than relying on full teacher demonstrations, which often create a mismatch between training and testing conditions. This method was tested across HotpotQA, ALFWorld, and Terminal-Bench-Dev, showing improved performance over traditional behavioral cloning at matched supervision budgets. The study frames on-policy data construction as a budget-allocation problem, exploring how to best allocate teacher output among start-to-finish demonstrations, continuation length, outcome filtering, and coverage of learner-induced contexts. Results indicate that short teacher continuations at learner-induced contexts can match or outperform more heavily filtered or longer teacher outputs, suggesting a more efficient use of supervision resources for fine-tuning LLM agents.

item.title: Researchers propose SaMer, an object-aware token merging method that compresses image tokens by over 93% while preserving object evidence for improved vision-language retrieval on Flickr30K and MSCOCO [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SaMer, an object-aware token merging method that significantly compresses image tokens by over 93% while maintaining critical object-level information for vision-language retrieval tasks. SaMer reduces storage requirements and improves retrieval accuracy on datasets like Flickr30K and MSCOCO by merging image tokens into representative centroids without losing important visual evidence needed for effective query matching. The method uses object annotations during training to guide token merging and avoids mixing tokens from different objects, but it does not require bounding boxes or detectors during inference. By adapting only the shared projection layer and keeping vision and language backbones frozen, SaMer achieves a 16-fold reduction in storage and outperforms existing compression techniques. This approach highlights the importance of preserving object evidence in efficient multi-vector retrieval systems, enabling better phrase-level grounding and improved retrieval performance.

item.title: Researchers propose Circadian Rhythm Score for depression screening and intervention, achieving 0.825 ROC-AUC on 15,233-person China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new Circadian Rhythm Score (CRS) to improve depression screening by integrating multiple daily behavioral indicators into a single, interpretable measure. Tested on data from 15,233 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, the CRS-based framework achieved a robust screening performance with an ROC-AUC of 0.825. This approach not only enhances prediction accuracy but also identifies actionable behavioral thresholds for interventions, such as recommended exercise levels and optimal nap durations for sleep-deprived individuals. The CRS compresses diverse behaviors like sleep, activity, and social interactions into a unified representation while preserving meaningful behavioral semantics. The researchers employed gradient-boosted trees and SHAP analysis to reveal complex relationships between circadian rhythms and depression risk. Additionally, the framework incorporates interaction modeling and counterfactual regression to estimate individualized and dose-dependent effects, supporting intervention-oriented decision-making under varying circadian contexts. By combining supervised representation learning with interpretable modeling, this work offers a scalable and practical tool for depression screening and personalized intervention planning, potentially advancing healthcare data mining and mental health management.

item.title: Researchers introduce ToolFailBench, a diagnostic benchmark analyzing tool-use failures in 19 large language models across 1,000 tasks in finance, medicine, law, cybersecurity, and real estate [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ToolFailBench, a diagnostic benchmark designed to analyze tool-use failures in large language models (LLMs) across 1,000 tasks spanning finance, medicine, law, cybersecurity, and real estate. Unlike aggregate benchmark scores that can obscure specific failures, ToolFailBench identifies distinct failure modes such as skipping necessary tool calls, ignoring tool results, fabricating outputs, and unnecessary tool use. The benchmark evaluates 19 prominent LLMs, revealing that even the best models achieve only an 86.33% clean tool-use rate, indicating room for improvement in faithful tool utilization. ToolFailBench differentiates between tasks that require tool use and control tasks that should be answered directly without tools, enabling a nuanced assessment of model behavior. The study found that models with similar overall accuracy often fail in different ways; for example, some models consistently avoid unnecessary tool calls, while others, like Llama-3.1 variants, tend to call tools indiscriminately. These findings suggest that evaluating LLMs should go beyond whether tools are called to also consider whether tool outputs are correctly used and whether tools are avoided when not needed.

item.title: Researchers propose Reward-Swap Policy Optimization (RSPO) to improve multi-turn LLM agent training by combining dense process rewards with outcome rewards, showing consistent gains on WebShop and ALFWorld benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Reward-Swap Policy Optimization (RSPO), a new method to enhance the training of large language models (LLMs) for multi-turn interactive tasks using reinforcement learning. RSPO addresses challenges in long-horizon tasks where sparse outcome rewards slow convergence and dense process rewards, while richer, may misalign with true outcomes. The approach combines dense process rewards with outcome rewards through a reward-swap mechanism, ensuring diverse trajectory sampling and alignment with true rewards to improve model performance. The team tested RSPO on the WebShop and ALFWorld benchmarks, applying it to various reinforcement learning algorithms such as GRPO, PPO, and GiGPO. Results showed consistent performance improvements across different baselines and tasks, demonstrating RSPO's effectiveness in leveraging dense feedback without compromising alignment with final outcomes.

item.title: Researchers propose Wasserstein residuals method for learning gradient flows from population dynamics, introducing a simulation-free particle-based stitching approach with state-of-the-art trajectory inference performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a new method called Wasserstein residuals for learning gradient flows from population dynamics, which models the evolution of distributions driven by an energy functional. Unlike traditional approaches based on the Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) scheme that require costly optimal transport computations and are limited by time discretization, this method uses a residual approach with a non-negative loss function to enforce continuity equations, resulting in a single global objective. This framework unifies existing methods and leads to a novel particle-based technique called stitching, which is simulation-free and effective even with large gaps between observations. The stitching method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on trajectory inference benchmarks, offering a robust and efficient alternative for reconstructing population dynamics. The approach combines the residual loss with a data-fitting divergence, enabling flexible and accurate modeling of dynamic distributions without the computational overhead of solving optimal transport problems. The researchers have made their code publicly available to facilitate further exploration and application of this technique.
